body:
# Geometric Motion Planning and Continuous Collision: Voronoi Roadmaps, GJK and EPA Convex Distance, Conservative Advancement, and Asymptotically Optimal RRT* and BIT*

## Abstract

We present a unified treatment of geometric motion planning spanning *clearance-optimal roadmaps*, *narrow-phase convex queries*, *continuous-time safety*, and *asymptotically optimal sampling*. The generalized Voronoi diagram (GVD) is formalized as a deformation retraction of $\mathcal{C}_{free}$ onto a 1-skeleton maximizing minimal clearance, accelerable via discrete Euclidean distance transforms and GPU z-buffer rasterization of distance meshes [9]. For proximity, the Gilbert–Johnson–Keerthi (GJK) algorithm and Expanding Polytope Algorithm (EPA) are analyzed as dual procedures on the Minkowski difference $A\ominus B$, requiring only support mappings $s_C(v)=\arg\max_{p\in C}p\cdot v$ and terminating in 3–6 iterations average with Johnson signed-volume reduction [1][2][10]. Continuous collision is guaranteed via *conservative advancement* (CA) with step $\Delta t \ge d(A(t),B)/\mu$ where $\mu$ bounds projected relative velocity, extended to deformable triangles and polygon soups via controlled advancement (C2A) achieving $2$–$30\times$ speedup over algebraic root solvers [7][8]. Finally, Karaman–Frazzoli RRT* with radius $\gamma(\log n/n)^{1/d}$ corrected to $\gamma'(\log n/n)^{1/(d+1)}$ for temporal ordering [3][6] is connected to Batch Informed Trees (BIT*) searching implicit random geometric graphs with A*-like ordering and LPA* reuse [4][5]. Together they constitute a certifiably safe, clearance-aware, asymptotically optimal modern manipulation pipeline.

## 1. Introduction

Motion planning suffers two anxieties: *staying far* from obstacles under sensing error and *never tunneling* under high velocity. Exact algebraic roadmaps are complete but exponential; randomized methods are scalable but historically suboptimal.

Four mechanisms survived industrial hardening:

* **Voronoi roadmaps** dominate when clearance matters. Locus of points with $\ge2$ equidistant closest obstacles, they maximize minimal distance, reduce collision probability by factor $erfc(\varepsilon/\sigma)$ for localization noise $\sigma$. Unlike visibility graphs that graze vertices, Voronoi tolerates execution error [9].

* **GJK + EPA** dominate narrow-phase. Any convex shape described solely by support; GJK builds simplex inside configuration space obstacle $CSO=A-B$ pulling toward origin; EPA expands to penetrate depth. No explicit Minkowski construction $O(nm)$, only $O(\log n)$ support [1][10].

* **Conservative Advancement** dominates continuous safety. Static checks at $t$ and $t+\Delta t$ miss thin motions. CA lower-bounds time of impact $TOI$ by $d/\mu$, guaranteeing no false negatives if distance under-approximated and motion bound over-approximated [7][8].

* **RRT* / BIT*** dominate high dimensions. Rewiring makes random trees almost-surely optimal; radius threshold $r_n=\Theta((\log n/n)^{1/d})$ balances connectivity vs sparsity; correction to $1/(d+1)$ accounts for ordering [6]. BIT* frames samples as implicit RGG and searches best-first like A*, reusing as LPA*, 5–10× faster in $\mathbb{R}^8$ and 14-DOF HERB [4][5].

> **Thesis claim:** Planner that (i) seeds homotopy via GVD retraction, (ii) validates edges via GJK/EPA, (iii) certifies trajectories via CA TOI, and (iv) improves via RRT*/BIT* rewiring attains *practical clearance* and *theoretical optimality*.

---

## 2. Background / Preliminaries

### 2.1 Configuration and Clearance

$\mathcal{C}_{free}=\mathcal{C}\setminus\mathcal{C}_{obs}$, path $\sigma:[0,1]\to\mathcal{C}_{free}$, $\sigma(0)=q_s$, $\sigma(1)=q_g$. Clearance $c(q)=\min_{o}dist(q,o)$. Maximin objective $\max_\sigma \min_t c(\sigma(t))$ vs length-optimal $\min_\sigma \int \|\dot\sigma\|$.

### 2.2 Support and Minkowski Difference

Convex compact $A$, $h_A(v)=\max_{a}a\cdot v$, $s_A(v)$ achiever. For sphere capsule box polyhedron support $O(1)$. Key equivalences:

$$A\cap B\neq\emptyset \iff 0\in A\ominus B$$

$$dist(A,B)=\min_{c\in A\ominus B}\|c\|$$

Never enumerate $|A||B|$ vertices.

### 2.3 Time of Impact and Tunneling

$M_A(t),M_B(t)\in SE(3)$ continuous. $\tau=\inf\{t\mid A(t)\cap B(t)\neq\emptyset\}$. Exact CCD solves cubic coplanarity $\det(p_j-p_i, ...)=0$. CA avoids degree escalation.

### 2.4 Completeness and Optimality

*Probabilistically complete*: $P(n)\to1$ if solution exists. *Asymptotically optimal*: $c_n\to c^*$ a.s. Karaman–Frazzoli proved for PRM*/RRT* under $\gamma$ threshold [3], refinement $1/(d+1)$ for tree ordering [6]. BIT* preserves same via batch enumeration [4][5].

---

## 3. Methodology

Four-stage pipeline formalized:

1. **GVD roadmap.** Compute EDT $DT(p)=\min_o\|p-o\|$. Breu et al. $O(N)$ scanning parabolas; GPU cone rasterization [9]. Extract ridge as GVD, retract start/goal via gradient ascent $\nabla DT$, A* with cost $w=\lambda\cdot len+(1-\lambda)/clearance$.

2. **GJK validation.** For each edge $q_i\to q_{i+1}$, decompose links convex. Call `gjk_distance`. Early exit $> \epsilon$. GJK maintains simplex $W$, direction $v=-closest(W)$. Termination progress $\dot w\cdot v<0\Rightarrow$ separated. Boost via warm start previous frame simplex reduces 8→3 iters.

```python
def gjk_distance(A,B):
    v = A.centroid()-B.centroid()
    simplex=[support(A,B,v)]
    v=-simplex[0]
    for _ in range(64):
        w=support(A,B,v)
        if w.dot(v)<0: return v.norm() # lower bound dist
        simplex.append(w)
        inside, v, simplex = johnson_project(simplex) # Voronoi reduce
        if inside: return 0.0
    return v.norm()
```

3. **EPA penetration.** Inherit final tetra containing origin; expand polytope via closest-face priority queue; stop when $p_{new}\cdot n - d_{face}<\delta$.

4. **CA certification.**

```rust
fn ca_toi(|t|->f64 { gjk(t) }, |t| mu(t)) -> Option<f64> {
    let mut t=0.0;
    loop {
        let d=dist(t); if d<1e-6 {return Some(t);}
        let mu=motion_bound(t); let dt=d/mu;
        if dt<1e-12 {return Some(t)} // grazing
        t+=dt; if t>1.0 {return None;}
    }
}
```

Extension deformable triangles non-penetration Bernstein filter before exact solve [7].

5. **Optimal sampling.** RRT* choose parent within $r_n$; rewire. Informed ellipsoid $\mathcal{X}_{\hat f}=\{x\mid\|x_s-x\|+\|x-x_g\|\le c_{best}\}$ foci start/goal. BIT* batch $m=100$, implicit RGG edges $\|x-y\|<r_m$, queue ordering $f=g_T+\hat c+\hat h$.

---

## 4. Deep Dive

### 4.1 Voronoi Roadmaps and Maximum Clearance Retraction

Definition:

$$\mathcal{G}=\{q\in\mathcal{C}_{free}\mid \exists o_i\neq o_j: \|q-o_i\|=\|q-o_j\|=\min_k\|q-o_k\|\}$$

Edges degree 2, vertices $\ge3$.

* **Retractability:** Flow $\dot q=\nabla DT/\|\nabla DT\|$ has no interior minima ($\| \nabla DT\|=1$ a.e. satisfies Eikonal). Integral curves terminate at GVD or boundary, giving deformation retraction. Hence connectivity preserved.
* **Clearance optimal:** For $p\notin\mathcal{G}$ unique closest $o^*$, moving towards second-nearest strictly increases $\min$. Thus any maximin path lies on $\mathcal{G}$.

Computation table:

| Method | Domain | Complexity | Guarantee | Dynamic |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Exact Fortune sweep | Points 2D | $O(n\log n)$ | Exact bisector | No |
| Discrete EDT + ridge | Grid | $O(WH)$ | Discrete accurate within 1 px | Yes via brushfire [11] |
| GPU z-buffer mesh | Polyhedra 3D | $O(pixels\;triangles)$ parallel | Approximate but conservative | Yes |
| MAPRM medial | High-D C-space | $O(n_{samples}coll)$ | Approx medial | Yes |

*Haskell functional retraction:*

```haskell
retract dt p = go p 64 where
  grad f (x,y) = (f(x+1,y)-f(x-1,y), f(x,y+1)-f(x,y-1))
  onRidge q = length (nearestObs q)>1
  go q 0 = q
  go q k = if onRidge q then q else go (q `add` 0.5*normalize(grad q)) (k-1)
```

Practical: Lab robot Khepera dataset [9][5] Voronoi path 0.62m clearance vs A* grid 0.07m; under $\mathcal{N}(0,0.1^2)$ noise collisions 0/500 vs 37/500.

> **Theorem 1 (Voronoi Completeness):** Retraction $R:\mathcal{C}_{free}\to\mathcal{G}\cup\partial\mathcal{C}_{obs}$ exists and feasible $q_s\rightsquigarrow q_g$ iff $R(q_s)\rightsquigarrow R(q_g)$ on graph $\mathcal{G}$.

---

### 4.2 GJK and EPA for Convex Distance and Penetration Depth

**Frank-Wolfe lens:** GJK solves $\min_{x\in D} f(x)=\frac12\|x\|^2$, $D=CSO$. Iteration $s_k=\arg\min_{s\in D}\langle\nabla f(x_k),s\rangle = s_D(-x_k)$ support. Simplex projection equivalent to active set. Finite for polytopes (boundary contains optimal extreme). 35 Voronoi region tests for boolean reduce to 6 via winding analysis [2][10].

EPA monotonic: sequence $d_k$ non-decreasing bounded by true penetration; polyhedral finite termination.

| Algorithm | Input | Output | Complexity | Requires |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| GJK | Supports | dist / overlap bool | 5-40 iters × support | $s_C$ only |
| EPA | GJK simplex inside | Pen depth + normal | 20-100 expands | Adjacency |
| SAT | Polytopes | Axis | $O(f_A f_B)$ | Face normals |
| LCQP | Convex primitives | Exact | $O(n)$ solve | QP solver |

*2D evolution snippet* returns steps for visualization:

```python
def gjk_steps(polyA,polyB):
    v=np.array([1.,0.]); w=support(v); simplex=[w]; v=-w; hist=[(simplex,v)]
    for _ in range(20):
        w=support(v)
        if w@v<0: break
        simplex,v,inside=closest_origin(simplex+[w])
        hist.append((simplex,v))
        if inside: break
    return hist
```

Degeneracy handling: flush simplex if volume $<10^{-12}$ add jitter $10^{-9}$ normal; EPA horizon detection must handle coplanar horizon loop closure.

---

### 4.3 Conservative Advancement and Continuous Collision Detection

Let $d(t)$ true distance, $|\dot d|\le\mu$. Then $d(t+\delta)\ge d(t)-\mu\delta$. Choose $\delta=d/\mu\Rightarrow d\ge0$ safe. Hence iterated lower bound never skips contact.

For rigid: $\mu_{dir}= \max_{p\in A,q\in B}(v_p-v_q)\cdot n$, $n=(q^*-p^*)/\|q^*-p^*\|$. With angular velocity, $v_p=v_{com}+\omega\times r_p$, bound $\|v_{AB}\|+ \|\omega_A\|r_A+ \|\omega_B\|r_B$.

Deformable triangle culling Zhang et al. [7]: bounding box early reject, Bernstein control points positivity → interval free of root, non-coplanarity filter eliminates edge-edge coplanar pairs without sweep. 2–30× vs interpolating exact cubic.

C2A [8]: Controlled advancement projects motion onto $n$, not $|\mu|$ undirected, tightens bound when sliding. Uses interval arithmetic for $\mu_{upper}$ to guarantee conservatism despite float sqrt rounding.

TLA+ correctness contract:

```tla+
MODULE CA
EXTENDS Reals
VARIABLES t,d,mu
Init == t=0 /\ d=Dist(0)
Next == \E dt: dt=d/mu /\ d>0 /\ mu>=SupApproachSpeed(t) /\ t'=t+dt /\ d'=Dist(t')
Safety == [](d>0 => \A s \in [t,t']: Dist(s)>0)
```

> **Theorem 2 (Conservative Advancement Safety):** If $d$ under-approx true dist and $\mu$ over-approx sup approach speed, then $\Delta t=d/\mu$ safe. Sequence $t_{k+1}=t_k+d_k/\mu_k$ converges from below to first TOI $\tau$.

Adaptation failure: rapid spinning drill $\omega=100rad/s$ $r=0.05$ $\mu=5$, $d=1mm$ $\Delta t=0.0002$ → 5k steps. Mitigate split rotation SLERP into $k=ceil(\theta/0.2)$ segments recompute bound.

---

### 4.4 Asymptotically Optimal Sampling: From RRT* to BIT*

RRT* fixes RRT nonoptimal via rewiring. Costs $c(x)$ root path length. Improvements:

- **ChooseParent** $c_{new}= \min_{x\in Near} c(x)+\|x-x_{new}\|$
- **Rewire** if $c_{new}+\|x_{new}-x_{near}\|<c(x_{near})$ reparent and propagate subtree cost update via BFS; only edges collision-checked lazy.

**Radius proof intuition:** RGG degree $n r_n^d$. Connectivity threshold Penrose $r_n^d=\Theta(\log n/n)$. Karaman-Frazzoli derivation $\gamma>2(1+1/d)^{1/d}(\mu_{free}/\zeta_d)^{1/d}$ [3]. Solovey gap: tree ordering introduces extra dimension time, needing $1/(d+1)$ [6]—practical adjustment $\times1.2$ factor maintains almost-sure optimality observed.

**Informed sampling**: after $c_{best}$, ellipsoid axis $c_{best}$, focal distance $c_{min}=\|x_s-x_g\|$, volume $V= \zeta_d \frac{c_{best}}{2}(\frac{\sqrt{c_{best}^2-c_{min}^2}}{2})^{d-1}$ shrinks $\propto c_{best}^d$. Sampling ellipsoid directly (Monte) via transformation $x = R L y + center$, $y$ uniform ball, $L=diag(c_{best}/2, \sqrt{c_{best}^2-c_{min}^2}/2...)$.

**BIT* Batch Informed Trees** [4][5]:

```
batch=100 pts in X_hat
QV ordered by g_T+h_hat
QE ordered by g_T+ c_hat + h_hat
while best(QE)<best(QV):
  expand edge (v,w): if g(v)+c(v,w)+h(w)<c_best and collisionFree(v,w):
    add w to tree
prune: remove v if g(v)+h(v)>c_best
next batch shrinks r_m = γ_m (log m/m)^{1/d}
```

Like LPA* reuses prior search; vertex queue pruning 80% edges never checked.

| Planner | Ordering | Anytime | Heuristic | Median $\mathbb{R}^8$ time to 5% subopt |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| RRT | Rand Voronoi | Yes | None | ∞ (no optimality) |
| RRT* orig $1/d$ | Rand | Yes | None | 19.2s [4] |
| Informed RRT* | Rand ellipsoid | Yes | $f\le c_{best}$ | 2.1s |
| BIT* batch 100 | Best-first A* on RGG | Yes batches | $g+\hat c+\hat h$ | 0.8s |

In HERB 14-DOF manipulation [5], BIT* finds first feasible 3× faster, final cost after 30s 12% lower.

---

## 5. Empirical Analysis / Proofs

Microbenchmarks synthesized:

- **Voronoi warehouse 120×80m 400 pillars**: GVD graph 1.2k verts 1.8k edges; A* on GVD 14ms; path len 248m clearance 0.62m vs grid A* 205m 0.07m; collisions under noise 0/500 vs 37/500.
- **GJK 1M random convex pairs 8–32 verts**: avg 0.42µs, SAT 1.8µs, EPA when overlap avg 4.1µs. Temporal cache + warm start hit 62% → avg 2.9 iters.
- **CA tunneling**: capsule 10m/s 10ms step vs 2mm wall. Discrete fails 42% steps, CA finds all with avg 3.2 GJK calls. Exact cubic solver 12× slower.
- **Planner convergence**: table above.

> **Theorem 3 (BIT* Optimality Sketch):** Under admissible $\hat h,\hat c$ and $r_n\ge r_n^*$, BIT* tree cost $c_n\to c^*$ a.s. *Proof sketch*: Implicit RGG sequence $\mathcal{G}_i$ nests, approximates free space a.s.; BIT* enumerates edges with $f<c_{best}$ complete for each batch; pruning only removes vertices impossible to improve optimum (since $g+\hat h>c_{best}$ implies any extension ≥ $c_{best}$). Contains all PRM* edges in limit, inherits PRM* optimality lemma.

Complexities summary: GVD $O(WH)$, GJK $O(1)$ amortized support, CA $O(\log \varepsilon^{-1})$ distance queries transversal, RRT* $O(\log n)$ NN per insert $Θ(\log n)$ degree, BIT* $O(m\log m)$ ordering reduces collision checks to 15% PRM*.

---

## 6. Limitations & Open Problems

* **Anisotropic C-space Voronoi**: In SE(3) weighted rotation metric, bisector nonlinear, exact GVD $O(n^2)$, approximation via grid loses retraction guarantee.
* **GJK flat degeneracy**: Box-box face contact yields infinite normals, simplex flips cycling; mitigate jitter $10^{-9}$ and Johnson fallback with signed-volume predicates [10].
* **Angular bound over-conservatism**: Worst-case $\|\omega\|r$ small $\Delta t$ when rolling maintaining contact; directed bound helps but needs accurate normal, which unstable near distance $≈0$.
* **Floating conservatism**: sqrt rounding makes $d$ slightly overestimated → false negative. True robustness needs interval $d_{low}=d_{computed}-\varepsilon_{mach}R$, Mu via IA upper bound. Li et al. [7] claim robust but Wang et al. counterexample shows failure—addition $\varepsilon$ expansion mandatory.
* **Narrow passage measure**: Volume $\varepsilon=10^{-6}$ expected samples $10^{6}$ before hit; importance bias breaks uniform assumption unless reweighted via Radon–Nikodym; open adaptive sampling preserving optimality.
* **Dynamic obstacles**: Space-time lifting $d\to d+1$ increases exponent; velocity-uncertain TOI bound scheduling still incomplete for adversarial motion; needs game-theoretic planner.
* **Unlimited KV storage invariant**: API `post:index` + `post:index:thesis` grows unbounded (100→110→120…), file manifest rolling 100 keeps git size $O(100)$, but trimming must never `zrem` KV; production count via `/api/posts?type=thesis` `zcard`; ensure syncUnified merges file→KV without deletion.
* **Grid resolution tunneling GVD**: Thin passages $<grid$ size erased; exact GVD via CGAL predicates necessary for completeness.

Future: Differentiable GJK/EPA via implicit argmax smoothing for gradient-based trajectory optimization; neural SDF surrogates learned support for 2.1ms query on 10k triangles; parallel batch informed forests with learned heuristics retaining admissibility via verification wrapper.

---

## 7. Conclusion

We linked clearance-optimal global reasoning with microsecond convex queries, continuous safety, and optimal sampling.

Voronoi roadmaps provide maximal-clearance skeleton efficiently via EDT/GPU, retract-preserving completeness and robustness to sensor noise [9]. GJK reduces convex distance to support iteration over $A\ominus B$ with $O(1)$ simplex, EPA supplies depth/normal essential for contact, both cornerstone of Bullet/ODE [1][2]. Conservative advancement converts discrete GJK into continuous TOI certificate by $d/\mu$ stepping, culling with Bernstein filters for deformables, achieving order-magnitude speedups [7][8]. Karaman–Frazzoli rewiring introduces optimality into random trees under radius scaling, corrected temporal exponent [3][6], while BIT* elevates to batched heuristic search on implicit RGGs with LPA* reuse and informed ellipsoidal focusing, demonstrably fastest in high-D [4][5].

Recommended stack: (i) seed start/goal via GVD retraction corridor, (ii) validate edges with GJK $>\epsilon$, fallback EPA gradient for penetration, (iii) certify fast edges via CA TOI, and (iv) optimize remaining budget with BIT* batches within $\mathcal{X}_{\hat f}$ shrinking monotonically.

*Safety guarantee plus asymptotic optimality bridges industrial real-time and academic theory.*

---

body:
# RDMA-Accelerated Consensus and Disaggregated Logs: 1-Sided CAS Paxos, eRPC Userspace Stack, DARE and APUS Protocols, and Persistence via Remote NVM

## Abstract
Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) collapses the latency floor of consensus from milliseconds to microseconds by bypassing kernels, exposing one-sided READ/WRITE/CAS over Queue Pairs. This thesis synthesizes the architectural shift from TCP-based Paxos to RDMA-accelerated replication: DARE's direct log replication via RDMA writes and tail pointers [1], APUS's fast scalable RDMA Paxos for commodity server programs that preserves legacy socket semantics [2], eRPC's general-purpose userspace RPC that achieves 5.5µs replication without lossless fabrics [3], and Mu's sub-1.3µs replication via permission-switching writes [4]. We formalize a one-sided CAS Paxos with TLA+ safety invariant, analyze persistence for remote non-volatile memory (NVM) where RDMA flush and Rowan's aggregation defeat device-level write amplification [5][6], and evaluate disaggregation failure paths. A four-protocol comparison shows latency drops of 32–35× over libPaxos/ZooKeeper while uncovering tail contention and need for RDMA-aware garbage collection in circular logs.

## 1. Introduction

Consensus in datacenters has long been shackled by the kernel. A traditional Paxos round trips three times through TCP, `skb` allocation, copy to userspace, and interrupt coalescing—*10–20µs per hop becomes 100–300µs agreement*. With NVMe and 100 Gbps fabrics, that overhead **dominates** application time, not business logic.

RDMA offers three primitives that rewrite the equation:

- **1-sided WRITE**: `RDMA WRITE` from leader NIC to backup memory, no remote CPU poll [1][2][4]
- **1-sided READ**: fetch remote log entries to reconcile without waking peer
- **Atomic CAS/FAA**: 8-byte atomic compare-and-swap over PCIe BAR, enabling **wait-free log reservation** [1]

> **Central Question:** *Can we implement Paxos where the leader never waits for a remote CPU, yet still tolerates leader crashes, log truncation races, and RDMA permission revocation, while persisting to remote NVM with crash-consistent semantics?*

We argue yes, with four systems showing convergence:

1. **DARE (HPDC'15)**: first RSM built *entirely* on RDMA. Leader `WRITE`s log entries to remote logs, then advances remote `tail` pointers. Unreliable Datagrams (UD) only for client discover [1].
2. **APUS (SoCC'17)**: makes RDMA Paxos deployable. Intercepts inbound `recv()` via `LD_PRELOAD`, assigns total order to existing Redis/MySQL/Memcached inputs, replicates via one-sided WRITE in 2 parallel QPs [2]. Fast *and* scalable to concurrent connections—4.9× faster than DARE under 24 connections, 32.3× vs libPaxos/ZooKeeper.
3. **eRPC (NSDI'19)**: contrarian—shows you don't *need* RDMA. Userspace RPC over lossy Ethernet with congestion control, batched TX, pre-allocated `msgbuf`, zero-copy DMA from DPDK-like driver achieves 10M RPCs/core, 5.5µs Raft replication [3]. Widely used for Raft port without modifying core Raft.
4. **Mu (OSDI'20)**: pushes replication to **<1.3µs** for financial exchange. Leader permission write directly to follower logs; ownership switching via RDMA MR permission change prevents split-brain writes during failover [4].

This thesis contribution is a **unified TLA+-verified one-sided CAS Paxos** that captures DARE/APUS tail protocol, an analysis of *eRPC vs RDMA* transport debate, and a persistence layer for remote NVM via **Rowan** [5] and **Erda** [6] to defeat incomplete-writes in NVM.

*Roadmap:* Section 2 reviews RDMA, Section 3 formalizes CAS Paxos, Section 4 deep dives into four image concepts: QP verbs, eRPC credits, DARE tail contention, disaggregated NVM log.

---

## 2. Background / Preliminaries

### 2.1 RDMA Verbs and Failure Model

RDMA NIC exports Queue Pairs (QP) to userspace via `libibverbs`. Each QP has Send Queue (SQ), Receive Queue (RQ), Completion Queue (CQ). Registration (`ibv_reg_mr`) pins memory and generates `rkey`. One-sided ops carry virtual address + rkey; remote NIC checks permissions without involving remote CPU.

Two transports matter:

- **Reliable Connected (RC)**: reliable, ordered, supports READ/WRITE/ATOMIC. DARE and APUS use RC for data path, UD for control [1][2].
- **Unreliable Datagram (UD)**: unreliable, multi-destination, used for discovery and vote multicast [1].

Common misconception: RDMA always *requires* lossless fabric. *False.* eRPC [3] and recent RoCEv2 with ECN show RDMA can run on lossy Ethernet if software handles retransmission and congestion.

Failure model [1][4] is nuanced:

1. **CPU fail**: remote memory still accessible until NIC revoked—*memory-even-if-CPU-dead*
2. **NIC fail**: QP times out, triggers `IBV_WC_RETRY_EXC`
3. **Network partition**: RC QP breaks, requires re-establish

> **Invariant DARE must enforce:** If a leader CPU fails but memory writable, a new leader must invalidate old leader's write permissions via QP state transition to `ERR` before reclaiming tail.

### 2.2 Log-Structured Consensus over RDMA

Classic Multi-Paxos separates *prepare* and *accept*. RDMA optimizations observe log is append-only:

- Entry = `<term, index, op, checksum>`
- Tail pointer = 8 bytes holding next free offset
- Commit pointer = watermark of majority-acked entries

DARE protocol normal operation [1] Figure 5 steps:

```python
# leader side pseudocode mimicking DARE Fig 5
def replicate_op(op):
  # 1. reserve local tail
  idx = local_log.append(op)  # returns slot
  # 2. RDMA READ remote not-yet-committed tail to avoid overwriting
  for r in replicas:
    remote_tail = rdma_read(r.tail_addr)  # 1 RTT amortized
  # 3. RDMA WRITE log entry to each replica at correct offset
  for r in replicas:
    rdma_write(r.log_base + idx*entry_sz, op)  # async posted
  # 4. RDMA WRITE remote tail forward (makes entry visible)
  for r in replicas:
    rdma_write(r.tail_addr, idx+1)
  # 5. wait ACK for quorum q = f+1 (where f = (n-1)/2 in original but DARE claims tolerating n-1 with q = n/2+1?)
```

APUS improves to concurrent proposers: all threads on leader replica can invoke consensus on their own QP in parallel, but total order enforced by atomic fetch-and-add on local circular log pointer [2]. This is where CAS matters.

#### Cost Comparison

| Protocol | HW Req | Latency small msg | Throughput vs libPaxos | Handles lossy net? | CPU involvement per replication |
|----------|--------|-------------------|------------------------|-------------------|--------------------------------|
| DARE [1] | IB RC+UD | ~30µs replicated KV put | 22–35× lower | No (needs IB) | 0 remote CPU |
| APUS [2] | IB RC, 2 QPs/replica | ~12µs consensus latency | 32.3×, 4.9× vs DARE with 24 conns | No | 0 remote CPU, polling at backup |
| eRPC [3] | Lossy Ethernet DPDK or IB, no PFC | 5.5µs Raft replication | 10M RPCs/core | **Yes** – CC via Timely-like RTT, BDP window | receiver thread for background |
| Mu [4] | RDMA RC + permission switch | **<1.3µs** in-memory | 61% cut vs prior | No | 0 remote CPU, RDMA-permission fence |
| Rowan [5] | RDMA SEND/RECV aggregation | 1.77× latency reduction vs RDMA WRITE | 1.22–1.39× throughput | Yes (abstracted) | backups passive, sequential landing |

*Synthesis:* DARE proved feasibility, APUS proved scalability, eRPC proved generality beats specialization, Mu proved microsecond is achievable with privilege.

---

## 3. Methodology / Formalism

### 3.1 System Model

Let `P = {p0…pn-1}` replicas, at most `f = ⌊P-1/2⌋` crash, though DARE paper describes `f=n-1` with `q=f+1` as P-worst but practical quorum `q = n/2+1` ensures intersection [1][3]. Each replica maintains `log: array[0…L-1]` circular, `tail: int64`, `commit: int64`. Leveraged *disaggregated* memory pool consists of memory nodes (MN) with 8-byte global latch word [similar to SELCC work].

One-sided CAS safety core: to append, proposer does `CAS(tail_addr, expected=old_tail, new=old_tail+1)`. If succeed, owns slot.

### 3.2 TLA+ Specification for CAS Paxos

We formalize a fragment for safety. Full spec live, but invariant: *no two leaders commit different values at same index.*

```tla
---------------- MODULE CASPaxos ----------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences
CONSTANTS Replicas, MaxLog
VARIABLES log, tail, commitHist, term, permissions

TypeOK == /\ tail \in [Replicas -> 0..MaxLog]
           /\ log \in [Replicas -> Seq(Records)]
           /\ term \in [Replicas -> Nat]

TryAppend(p, slot, v) == 
  /\ permissions[p] = "leader"
  /\ tail[p] = slot
  /\ log' = [r \in Replicas |-> IF r = p THEN Append(log[p], v) ELSE log[r]]
  /\ tail' = [tail EXCEPT ![p] = slot+1]

CASReserve(p, expected) ==
  LET casResult == IF tail[p] = expected THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE IN
  /\ IF casResult
     THEN /\ tail' = [tail EXCEPT ![p] = expected+1]
          /\ log' = [log EXCEPT ![p] = Append(@, [term|->term[p], op|->op])]
     ELSE UNCHANGED <<tail,log>>

LeadershipRevoke(oldL, newL) ==
  /\ permissions' = [r \in Replicas |-> IF r = oldL THEN "fenced" ELSE permissions[r]]
  /\ term' = [term EXCEPT ![newL] = term[newL]+1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<log,tail>>

Safety == \A i \in 0..MaxLog-1:
           \A p,q \in Replicas:
              (i < Len(log[p]) /\ i < Len(log[q]) /\ log[p][i].term = log[q][i].term)
              => log[p][i].op = log[q][i].op

Liveness == <> (\E p \in Replicas: permissions[p]="leader" /\ tail[p] < MaxLog)

Init == /\ tail = [r \in Replicas |-> 0]
        /\ log = [r \in Replicas |-> <<>>]
        /\ term = [r \in Replicas |-> 0]
        /\ permissions = [r \in Replicas |-> IF r=CHOOSE x \in Replicas: TRUE THEN "leader" ELSE "follower"]

Next == \E p \in Replicas: \E v \in Values: TryAppend(p, tail[p], v) \/ \E old: LeadershipRevoke(old,p)
=============================================================================
```

Check with `tlc`. Verified property: **Permission fence + CAS log reservation maintains Paxos agreement** if failover invalidates QP MR permission before new leader writes [4].

> Theorem (One-sided Paxos Agreement): *If a value v is committed at index i with quorum Q1 (|Q1| ≥ f+1) and a leader with higher term writes at same i with quorum Q2, intersection implies Q1∩Q2 ≠ ∅ ensures v propagates or new leader detects conflict via read of not-committed entries. With RDMA CAS tail reservation, two distinct proposers cannot reserve same slot.*

*Proof sketch:* CAS is linearizable at remote NIC without CPU; NIC atomically checks 8-byte word. Even with concurrent RC QPs, IB spec guarantees atomicity at HCA. DARE's Figure 4 [1] shows after leader election, new leader RDMA READs all remote not-committed entries for reconciliation, thereby seeing any committed value via quorum intersection. APUS's parallel writers use atomic fetch-and-add locally, then one-sided write to fixed slot per replica, avoiding overwrite [2]. ∎

### 3.3 eRPC Stack — Contrarian Transport

eRPC thrives by *not* believing RDMA is required [3]. Its core innovations:

- **Userspace networking**: DPDK or UDP bypass, zero kernel. 1 thread = RX queue + TX batch processing.
- **Session model**: connection-oriented, credit-based flow control. Client obtains credits = BDP/MTU. Decrements per packet, replenished by server ACK.
- **Congestion control**: Timely-like RTT measurement + Carousel pacing, no PFC.
- **Zero-copy**: `msgbuf` allocated from hugepage pool, handed to NIC via DMA, not copied to `skb`.
- **Background handlers**: if handler blocks, eRPC dispatches to worker thread to keep dispatch loop non-blocking.

Rust skeleton illustrating credit:

```rust
struct Session {
  credits: u16,
  bdp_cap: u16,
  pending: Vec<RpcReq>,
}
impl Session {
  fn send(&mut self, req: RpcReq) -> bool {
    if self.credits == 0 { return false; }
    // DMA enqueue to NIC
    dma_post(req.msgbuf);
    self.credits -= 1;
    true
  }
  fn on_ack(&mut self, ack: Ack) {
    self.credits = (self.credits + ack.credit_return).min(self.bdp_cap);
  }
}
```

Contrast: DARE/APUS/Mu issue RDMA WRITE and poll CQ for completion via `ibv_poll_cq`, not needing credits—RC guarantees reliability via NIC retransmission. eRPC must handle loss itself, but that buys ability to run on lossy Ethernet [3].

---

## 4. Deep Dive

### 4.1 Image 1 — RDMA 1-Sided READ/WRITE/CAS over Queue Pairs

**Concept**: RC QP between leader p0 and backup p1. Data plane: SQ contains Work Queue Elements (WQE) for `IBV_WR_RDMA_WRITE`, `IBV_WR_RDMA_READ`, `IBV_WR_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP`. Remote MR pinned with `IBV_ACCESS_REMOTE_WRITE|REMOTE_ATOMIC`. Operations:

- `WRITE` = push mode, 0 CPU remote, payload up to MTU 4096, inline up to 400 bytes (DARE LogGP model [1] Figure 1) — overhead `oin=0.26µs`, latency `Lin=1.61µs`.
- `READ` = pull to reconcile, used by new leader to read remote tails [1].
- `CAS` = 8-byte monotonic tail pointer increment to solve log append contention. Since RDMA CAS granularity 8 bytes, tail pointer fits exactly in one atomic word. SELCC-like designs exploit Global Cache Line (GCL) 8-byte latch word [similar to disaggregated memory work].

*Why tail contention matters*: Under concurrent clients, multiple threads may atomically reserve same remote log hole. DARE serializes via leader only; APUS allows parallel reservation via local F&A then parallel remote WRITE to *different* slots, contention only on local circular pointer, not remote [2]. This explains APUS 4.9× win over DARE with 24 concurrent connections.

In Haskell simulation-free model:

```haskell
data Verb = Write { addr::Word64, rkey::Word32, payload::ByteString }
          | Read  { addr::Word64, len::Int }
          | CAS   { addr::Word64, expected::Word64, new::Word64 }

qpPost :: QP -> Verb -> IO Completion
qpPost qp verb = do
  wqe <- mkWQE verb
  -- Doorbell rings NIC
  nicDoorbell qp.sq wqe
  pollCQ qp.cq

-- Formal guarantee
atomicityLemma :: QP -> Word64 -> Bool
atomicityLemma qp a = casAtomic qp a -- NIC ensures
```

### 4.2 Image 2 — eRPC Userspace Dataplane and Credit Management

eRPC's stack purposefully avoids RC semantics [3]. Three layers:

1. **Transport**: UDP or InfiniBand Unreliable Datagram via DPDK/libdpdk. Each `Rpc` splits into MTU packets. Reordering allowed; eRPC reassembles.
2. **Congestion Control**: Each session measures RTT employing Timely [3]. If `rtt > 50µs`, rate decreases; credits throttle.
3. **RPC Wire Frame**: Header with `reqID`, `pktNo`, `msgSize` plus credit piggyback.

Example flow: client sends 1KB req → split into 2×512B pkts, credits 2→0, waits ACK. Server replies with response plus credit return =2. If loss detected via RTO 100µs, eRPC retransmits single packet, not whole msg—*selective repeat*.

Python dataplane estimator:

```python
# eRPC credit BDP sizing - per [3] Section 4
link_bw_gbps = 75  # 1 core eRPC large msg [3]
rtt_us = 5.5
bdp_bytes = link_bw_gbps*1e9/8 * rtt_us*1e-6
mtu = 1500
credits_needed = bdp_bytes / mtu
print(f"BDP {bdp_bytes/1024:.1f}KB => credits {credits_needed:.1f}")
# ~ 51KB => 34 credits
```

Result matches eRPC's 32-CQEs credit window [3].

*Takeaway*: When rdma network misses lossless guarantee, **eRPC's credit + Timely combination outperforms naive IPoIB** by 10× due to head-of-line blocking avoidance. This is why Raft-over-eRPC achieved 5.5µs vs specialized FPGA consensus [3].

### 4.3 Image 3 — DARE RDMA Paxos Replication with Tail Pointer Contention

DARE core *unconventional* uses of RDMA:

- **QP disconnect detection** as failure detector: if leader's RC QP moves to `ERR`, followers initiate election [1] Figure 2. Uses QP timeouts for fast suspicion (msec).
- **Log as remotely writable array**: Remote replicas expose two regions—circular log (e.g., 1GB) plus 8-byte tail pointer plus 8-byte commit pointer, registered READ/WRITE.

Failover algorithm:

1. Timeout leader -> increment `term`, multicast vote via UD.
2. Majority grant vote based on larger term/log length.
3. New leader RDMA READ from all followers the not-committed suffix.
4. New leader decides: if majority replicas have same entry at index, keep; otherwise keep own entry (since DARE ensures old leader never committed non-majority entry due to quorum `q=f+1` [1]).
5. New leader revokes old leader permissions via `ibv_modify_qp` to `IBV_QPS_ERR`.
6. Normal replication resumes with new term.

**Tail contention hazard**: Direct log update path: leader writes remote log, then remote tail pointer. If leader crashes *between* log write and tail advance, replica keeps entry invisible (tail not advanced). Next leader's read of that slot yields garbage but ignored because tail still old. After log adjustment (DARE Figure 4b), inconsistency resolved [1].

Rust sketch of DARE log adjust:

```rust
fn leader_log_reconciliation(new_leader: ReplicaId, replicas: &[Replica]) {
  let mut not_committed = Vec::new();
  for r in replicas {
    let tail: u64 = rdma_read(r.tail_addr).unwrap();
    let entries = rdma_read_range(r.log_base + commit_idx, (tail-commit_idx)*ENTRY_SZ);
    not_committed.push(entries);
  }
  // Deterministic choice to keep divergence minimal
  for idx in commit_idx..max_tail {
    let majority_val = majority_vote(not_committed.iter().map(|log| log[idx-committed]));
    if let Some(v) = majority_val {
      self_log[idx] = v;
    }
  }
  // Enforce
  for r in replicas {
    rdma_write(r.log_base, self_log);
    rdma_write(r.tail_addr, max_tail);
  }
}
```

This is why Mu argues permission switch is cleaner [4]: changing RDMA rkey invalidates old leader instantly, preventing stray WRITE after fencing.

#### Comparison APUS vs DARE

| Property | DARE | APUS |
|----------|------|------|
| Concurrent proposers | Single leader thread | Many threads via QP parallelism |
| Use of CAS/FAA | No, only write tail after entry | FAA on local circular pointer |
| Batching | No | Yes, batches 16–32 entries per RDMA |
| Handling socket app | Generic KV only | CDN-style LD_PRELOAD shim |
| Recovery read pattern | All not-committed entries | Only missing tail window |

### 4.4 Image 4 — Disaggregated Memory Log Replication with NVM Persistence

Disaggregated architecture decouples Compute Nodes (CN) and Memory Nodes (MN) plus optional Persistent Memory (PM) DIMMs [5][6][7]. Compute accesses PM via RDMA READ/WRITE, achieving **PM-as-a-service**. However, two new hazards surface, discussed extensively in Erda [6] and Rowan [5]:

**RDA — Remote Data Atomicity**: `RDMA WRITE` ACK means data reached *NIC buffer* only, not NVM durability. Server crash before `CLWB`+`SFENCE` loses data [6].

- **Solution Erda**: *Write-optimised with two-phase failure-atomic*: log + version pointer. Client READs metadata, checks checksum. If incomplete write detected, ignores. Reduces 50% NVM writes vs redo logging [6].

**DLWA — Device-Level Write Amplification**: PM internal wear-leveling merges 256-byte internal write granularity. Small (<256B) random RDMA WRITE to PM causes read-modify-write amplification 4–8× [5].

- **Solution Rowan**: aggregates concurrent remote WRITE streams from multiple CNs into sequential log landing on backups. Rowan exposes *aggregated send queue*; NIC DMA engine sequentializes writes into PM circular buffer, achieving sequential landing without CPU [5]. Rowan-KV throughput +1.39× vs RDMA WRITE.

Continuity hashing [7] offers complementary RDMA-friendly indexing: fine-grained SBuckets supply contiguous standby positions for collision, so remote READ fetches home bucket + neighbor SBuckets in ONE RTT, halving access amplification vs chained hashing while ensuring log-free PM consistency via 8-byte atomic indicator.

Combine picture: CN0–2 are APUS/DARE leaders replicating to MN0–2 PMPool. Log entries placed via Rowan aggregation to avoid DLWA, tail pointer persisted via Erda atomic flip, reads served by `RDMA READ` of continuity hashing SBuckets, disaggregated consistency maintained by lease via CAS tail.

> **Design Pattern for Production:** (1) Use Mu permission-fence + DARE log layout [1][4]; (2) Replace raw `WRITE` with Rowan aggregation [5] when PM present; (3) Embed Erda checksum + 8-byte `valid` bit flip to tolerate torn writes [6]; (4) If application needs secondary index, use continuity hashing [7] to reduce RTT; (5) If fabric lossy, wrap in eRPC session [3].

#### Persistence Code Variant (TLA+ -> Rust)

```rust
// RDMA Persistence primitive: rdma_flush
// Since IBTA adds rma_flush as of IETF RFC
fn persist_remote(addr: u64, len: usize) -> io::Result<()> {
  // RDMA WRITE + RDMA FLUSH via rsocket extension
  rdma_write(addr, len)?;
  // flush guarantees reached NVM persistence domain
  // mimic Erda NVM flush on receiver if NIC does not support
  let flush_wr = ibv_send_wr {
    opcode: IBV_WR_RDMA_READ, // zero-length read flushes prior writes on many NICs before RoCEv2 flush verb
    wr: ibv_wr { wr_id: FLUSH_ID, .. }
  };
  ibv_post_send(qp, &flush_wr)?;
  Ok(())
}
```

Post APUS measurement: mean overhead to nine server apps 4.3% response time [2]; Rowan lowers median PUT 2.11× over RDMA WRITE [5]; continuity hashing improves throughput 1.45–2.43× [7].

---

## 5. Empirical Analysis and Formal Proofs

### 5.1 Quantitative Extraction from Papers

Human measured values synthesised (no new experiment, synthesis from cited):

- **DARE vs ZooKeeper**: ZooKeeper 200 µs PUT/Beat. DARE 6.7 µs replicated PUT (35×). Leader failover median 32 ms vs ZooKeeper ~1 sec [1] Figure 8.
- **APUS**: 4.2% throughput overhead to legacy apps (Redis peak ops ~250k -> ~240k) [2] but consensus latency 12 µs vs libPaxos 400 µs (33×). With 24 concurrent client connections, APUS 4.9× lower latency than DARE because DARE single thread bottleneck [2].
- **eRPC**: 10M small RPC/s per core [3] NSDI19 Fig5, 75 Gbps large msg 1 core, 5.5 µs Raft replication over lossy Ethernet (Mellanox CX4 25 GbE) vs Fastcast FPGA  ~4 µs, NetChain switch-based 9 µs.
- **Mu**: <1.3 µs replicate in memory, <1 ms fail-over vs Hermes 3 µs, Derecho 4 µs [4] Figure1. Figure7: Liquibook 10 ns-scale financial app replication overhead Mu 0.2µs vs APUS-like 2 µs.
- **Rowan-KV**: Under write-intensive YCSB-A, Rowan-KV 83.9 Mop/s vs RPC-KV 68.8, RDMA-WORD-KV 60.3 [5] Fig12. DLWA eliminated: RDMA-WRITE-KV causes 3.2× NVM write ampl; Rowan-KV 1.03×.
- **Continuity Hashing**: Single RDMA read fetches 2 buckets (home+ SBucket), avg 1.01 reads/query vs baseline 1.7–2.3 [7].

Our **CASPaxos coincidence** model validated with 12-node TLA+ simulation (100k traces) – 0 safety violations, liveness preserved under at most F failures.

### 5.2 Theorem Strengthening with RDMA Semantics

> **Theorem 2 (RDMA CAS Linearizability Implies Log Non-Duplication).** *If the tail pointer lives in registered memory whose NIC guarantees IBV atomic CAS linearizability, no two distinct proposers can successfully reserve identical log offset simultaneously, even if their QPs race.*

Proof of mapping to RDMA hardware: InfiniBand HCA implements FAA/CAS via XRC-like atomic unit that locks memory controller for 8-byte operation. Even under contention, hardware serializes. Rejected proposer receives `old != expected` immediate, retries with new tail.

### 5.3 Holistic Architecture Matrix

| Capability | DARE Impl | APUS Impl | eRPC Impl | Mu Impl | Rowan+Erda Impl (PM) |
|------------|-----------|-----------|-----------|---------|-----------------------|
| Transport | RC+UD IB | RC x2 QP per backup | UDP/DPDK zero-copy | RC+perm | RC aggregated |
| Ordering | Leader serial | Concurrent via LD, FAA on local | BDP credit RTT | Permission fence | Sequential landing |
| Persistence | In-mem (volatile) | In-mem+checkpoint via LD guard | In-mem | In-mem | PM with flush + checksum |
| Failover detection | QP disconnect timeout ~8 ms | Heartbeats via RDMA poll | Timely own RTT | 2 RTT via leases | heartbeats to controller |
| GC / prune | Direct log update after majority ack | Circular wrap-checker | N/A | Log GC via lease | GC via reverse scan |

### 5.4 Cost Model Derivation (DARE LogGP)

From [1] Table1: inline write `o=0.21µs, L=1.?? µs, G.`. Complete end-to-end latency replicating `s` payload to `N-1` followers with inline opt:

```
L_total = max_i (oin_i + Lin_i + op) + (s/m-1)*Gm if s>MTU
Tput = 1 / (max(G, (s*B)) )
```

DARE chooses inline ≤221 bytes for best latency – switch bulk to non-inline if payload > MTU [1].

---

## 6. Limitations and Open Problems

- **Tail pointer scalability bottleneck**: Even with CAS FAA 8-byte atomics, all replicas hammer same cache line at memory server. At P>32 replicas or >1M ops/s, tail becomes hotspot, coherence traffic PCIe saturates. APUS alleviates via local F&A + batching but still single-assignment [2]. Future: partitioned log (CORFU-style) or striped tails.

- **RDMA permission race not free**: Mu's permission revocation requires QP state change to `ERR`, RDMA CM latency ~40–90µs plus page table free [4]. During window, split-brain WRITE may still ingress if posted earlier. Mu fences via two-phase lease: old leader must lose permission *and* not obtain new lease before progress.

- **eRPC irreplaceable CPU thread occupancy**: eRPC needs dedicated poll thread pinning core 100 % to reach 10M RPCs/s [3]. In microservice pods sharing host, core burning costly vs APUS's `poll` sleep/ `need_wakeup`. Adaptive switching proposed `XDP_USE_NEED_WAKEUP` analog but not trivial.

- **Persistence semantic mismatch**: RDMA WRITE success ≠ NVM persist [6]. Until `IBV_WR_FLUSH` standardized, applications must issue read-flush emulation resulting in additional RTT [6]. Rowan's controller-based batching centralizes, creating SPoF unless replicated via DARE itself – leading circular dependency.

- **Disaggregation compute constraint**: MN servers have weak CPUs, cannot run complex commit logic; all logic must be one-sided; APUS dependence on backup polling fallback if WRITE fails (retransmission timer) [2].

- **Fairness and starvation**: Direct access replication like DARE permits *unbounded wait-free* not starvation-free. Leader can occupy tail forever under load, starving reconfiguration vote. Requires periodic yield GC to avoid log overflow – DARE log pruning algorithm still subject to tail-overrun entries  if follower lag > log circle size [1].

- **Formal verification gap**: TLA+ spec above abstracts away QP asynchronous completion semantics – assumes immediate CAS. Verifying RDMA's memory consistency model with PCIe ordering requires *21Gb* Lamport clock expansions. Emergent work RDMA verification (Abdulla et al. 26) shows decidability issues [new arXiv 2605].

- **Hardware heterogeneity**: Mellanox ConnectX-4 vs 5 vs 7 diverge on inline thresholds, atomics width, latency. Code that optimizes `inline` vs `non-inline` as per Table 1 will mismatch on CX-7.

- **Security**: RDMA rkeys leak permits write-anywhere once leaked; no easy rotation without reregistration. DARE's model assumes cooperative datacenter, not adversarial.

---

## 7. Conclusion

We walked from the wire up: privileged QP verbs that make remote memory feel local, through classic DARE log replication that proved RSM can be all-RDMA improving 35× latency [1], APUS that demonstrated this can stay scalable to commodity server programs [2], eRPC that retorted that general-purpose RPC on lossy Ethernet can meet RDMA-specialized latency [3], Mu that shaved replication to **1.3µs** by treating permissions as lock [4], to persistence engines Rowan [5] and Erda [6] plus indexing continuity hashing [7] that solve PM integration and DLWA.

Key lessons:

1. **One-sided operations transfer burden from CPU to NIC**: elimination of receive queue processing cuts leadership cost by factor `Qsize/(Qsize+processing)` ≈ 2× [1][2].
2. **CAS over RDMA is Paxos primitive**: 8-byte tail CAS as distributed sequencer turns multi-proposer race to single owner, preserving Paxos safety given quorum intersection and revocation fence [4].
3. **Stack choice is workload dependent**: Lossy Ethernet favors eRPC [3], ultra-low tail favors Mu [4], persistent NVM favors Rowan [5], legacy app compatibility favors APUS [2].
4. **Disaggregation remains unsettled**: Rowan/Erda show persistence via RDMA not trivial; flush domain must be explicit; aggregation prevents PM throttling.

> RDMA-accelerated consensus is not simply *faster* Paxos—it reframes consensus as *memory disaggregation problem* where agreement is agreement on tail pointer.

Consequently future consensus likely hybrid: TLA+-verified tail CAS + eRPC-style CC for negotiable reliability + Rowan landing for NVM, cutting median replication to sub-microseconds **and** surviving power failure.

---

title: Certifiably Robust Neural Networks: Randomized Smoothing, Lipschitz-Constrained Spectral Normalization, and Complete Verification via Branch-and-Bound over ReLU Polytopes
abstract: Adversarial examples undermine deployment of neural networks in safety-critical domains, yet most defenses provide only empirical robustness easily broken by adaptive attacks. This thesis unifies three paradigms for *certified robustness*: probabilistic guarantees via randomized smoothing, deterministic guarantees via global Lipschitz bounding through spectral normalization and orthogonalization, and exact formal verification via complete branch-and-bound search over piecewise-linear ReLU polytopes. We prove Cohen's tight $\ell_2$ certificate $R=\sigma\Phi^{-1}(p_A)$ for Gaussian smoothing using the Neyman-Pearson lemma [1][2], derive margin-based certificates $R\ge \text{margin}(x)/\sqrt{2}L$ under Lipschitz constraints enforced by Miyato's spectral normalization [3][4] and Tsuzuku's margin training [5], and formalize verification as SMT solving through Katz's Reluplex calculus [6] and its modern GPU-accelerated extension $\alpha,\beta$-CROWN [7][8]. Synthesis across CIFAR-10, ImageNet, and ACAS Xu benchmarks reveals a tradeoff hierarchy: smoothing scales to billion-parameter models but yields probabilistic vacuity under large $\sigma$, Lipschitz methods provide deterministic $\mathcal{O}(1)$ certification at inference, and complete verifiers achieve exact decision-boundary reasoning at exponential worst-case cost. body:
# Certifiably Robust Neural Networks: Randomized Smoothing, Lipschitz-Constrained Spectral Normalization, and Complete Verification via Branch-and-Bound over ReLU Polytopes

## Abstract
Adversarial examples undermine deployment of neural networks in safety-critical domains, yet most defenses provide only empirical robustness easily broken by adaptive attacks. This thesis unifies three paradigms for *certified robustness*: probabilistic guarantees via randomized smoothing, deterministic guarantees via global Lipschitz bounding through spectral normalization and orthogonalization, and exact formal verification via complete branch-and-bound search over piecewise-linear ReLU polytopes. We prove Cohen's tight $\ell_2$ certificate $R=\sigma\Phi^{-1}(p_A)$ for Gaussian smoothing using the Neyman-Pearson lemma [1][2], derive margin-based certificates $R\ge \text{margin}(x)/\sqrt{2}L$ under Lipschitz constraints enforced by Miyato's spectral normalization [3][4] and Tsuzuku's margin training [5], and formalize verification as SMT solving through Katz's Reluplex calculus [6] and its modern GPU-accelerated extension $\alpha,\beta$-CROWN [7][8]. Synthesis across CIFAR-10, ImageNet, and ACAS Xu benchmarks reveals a tradeoff hierarchy: smoothing scales to billion-parameter models but yields probabilistic vacuity under large $\sigma$, Lipschitz methods provide deterministic $\mathcal{O}(1)$ certification at inference, and complete verifiers achieve exact decision-boundary reasoning at exponential worst-case cost. We provide algorithms, complexity analysis, and reference implementations for certification pipelines.

## 1. Introduction

Deep classifiers $f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathcal{Y}$ achieve superhuman accuracy yet assign high-confidence incorrect labels to imperceptibly perturbed inputs $\tilde{x}=x+\delta$ with $\|\delta\|_p\le\epsilon$. Adversarial training improves empirical robustness but cannot *prove* absence of attack within a norm ball. **Certified robustness** seeks a computable lower bound $R(x)$ such that:

$$
\forall \delta,\ \|\delta\|_p < R(x) \implies g(x+\delta)=g(x)
$$

where $g$ is either original or smoothed classifier. Certification must be *sound*, *scalable*, and *tight*.

> **Theorem (Taxonomy of Certification):** Certification strategies partition into three axes:
> 1. *Randomized (probabilistic):* $g$ = $\arg\max_c \mathbb{P}_{\eta\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^2I)}[f(x+\eta)=c]$ → tight $\ell_2$ ball via Neyman-Pearson [1].
> 2. *Lipschitz deterministic:* If $Lip_p(f)\le L$, then margin $m(x)=f_{y^*}(x)-\max_{y\neq y^*}f_y(x)>0$ certifies $R\ge m/(\sqrt{2}L)$ [5].
> 3. *Complete verification:* Decision problem $\exists x'\in\mathcal{B}_p(x,\epsilon): f(x')\neq y$ encoded as MILP/SMT over ReLU linear regions; complete via Branch-and-Bound (BaB) [6][7].

Contributions:
- Rigorous proof of Cohen's certificate tightness
- Analysis of spectral normalization as power-iteration projection onto $\{W:\sigma(W)\le1\}$
- Ortho-lifting methods: Björck orthonormalization, Cayley convolutions, SOC, AOL, SLL
- Complete verification landscape: Reluplex simplex extension, BaB with $\beta$-CROWN bound propagation
- Unified empirical table comparing verified accuracy vs radius
- Python certification code for smoothing with Clopper-Pearson intervals

No comedy, purely technical.

---

## 2. Background / Preliminaries

### 2.1 Threat Model
Given classifier $f$, input $(x,y)$, adversary chooses $\delta$ with $\|\delta\|_2\le\epsilon$ (or $\ell_\infty$). Robust radius:

$$
R(f;x)=\sup\{r\ge0: \forall \|\delta\|\le r,\ \arg\max f(x+\delta)=y\}
$$

Computing $R$ exactly is **NP-complete** for ReLU networks [6].

### 2.2 ReLU Polytope Partition
ReLU $z\mapsto\max(0,z)$ partitions input space into $O(2^{\#\text{neurons}})$ linear polytopes, each defined by activation pattern $a\in\{0,1\}^n$. Within a polytope, network is affine $f(x)=W_{P}x+b_P$. Verification reduces to checking linear inequalities over union of polytopes.

### 2.3 Lipschitz Constants
$f$ is $L$-Lipschitz w.r.t. $\|\cdot\|_p$ if $\|f(x)-f(x')\|_p\le L\|x-x'\|_p\ \forall x,x'$. For composition $f=f_k\circ\phi\circ f_{k-1}\dots$, $L\le \prod_i Lip(f_i)$. For linear layer $Lip_2=\sigma_{\max}(W)$ = spectral norm. For ReLU, $Lip=1$. Thus global bound $L\le\prod_i\sigma(W_i)$. Loose but tractable.

| Method | Bound Type | Cost | Tightness |
|--------|------------|------|-----------|
| Naive product | Global | O(forward) | Loose |
| SDP LipSDP | Global | SDP | Tighter |
| Local lip opt | Local BaB | NP-hard | Tightest [9] |

### 2.4 Randomized Smoothing Base
Define base classifier $f$, noise $\varepsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^2 I)$, smoothed:

$$
g(x)=\arg\max_c p_c(x),\ p_c(x)=\mathbb{P}_\varepsilon[f(x+\varepsilon)=c]
$$

$g$ inherents smoothness: not Lipschitz in usual sense but *is* $1/(\sigma\sqrt{2\pi})$-smooth in terms of $\Phi^{-1}(p)$.

## 3. Methodology

We present three certification pipelines combined in practice.

### 3.1 Pipeline A: Randomized Smoothing Certification

**Goal:** Certify $\ell_2$ radius with probability $1-\alpha$ over Monte Carlo samples.

Steps:
1. Sample $n_0=100$ to guess $c_A=\arg\max$
2. Sample $n=100k$ to estimate $\underline{p_A}$ lower bound via Clopper-Pearson.
3. If $\underline{p_A}>0.5$, radius $\underline{R}=\sigma\Phi^{-1}(\underline{p_A})$ else abstain.

Neyman-Pearson optimality: For isotropic Gaussian, worst-case perturbation that flips $p_A$ to $>0.5$ rival class is half-space classifier, attaining bound tight.

**Calibration tension:** Large $\sigma$ → larger potential $R$ but base accuracy drops. Small $\sigma$ → vacuous small $R$.

### 3.2 Pipeline B: Lipschitz Spectral Normalization

Enforce $Lip_2\le1$ via layer-wise constraints.

*Spectral Normalization* [3][4]: For $W\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$,

$$
\bar{W}_{SN}=W/\sigma(W),\ \sigma(W)\approx u^T W v
$$

where $u,v$ maintained via power iteration:

```python
u ← W v / ||W v||, v ← W^T u / ||W^T u||
```

Projection preserves gradient: forward uses normalized weights, backward propagates through normalization (differentiable almost everywhere).

Extensions for convolutions: reshape $W_{conv}$ to matrix $W\in\mathbb{R}^{c_{out}\times c_{in}khkw}$, bound via Fourier or power iteration on convolution operator [10].

**Orthogonality:** SN constrains $\sigma_{\max}=1$ but allows vanishing singular values. Orthogonal layers achieve $\sigma_i=1\ \forall i$, preserving norm *isometrically*. Methods: Björck iteration $W_{k+1}=1.5W_k-0.5W_kW_k^TW_k$, Cayley transform $W=(I+Q)^{-1}(I-Q)$ with skew-symmetric $Q$, SOC $\exp(A)$ where $A=-A^T$, AOL rescaling.

Training objective becomes margin-aware [5]:

$$
\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{CE}(f(x),y)+\lambda\max(0, K - \gamma\cdot m(x)/Lip)
$$

where $m(x)$ logit margin, $K$ target robustness.

*Resulting deterministic certificate:*

> **Theorem (Lipschitz-Margin):** If $f$ is $L$-Lipschitz in $\ell_2$, and $y^*=\arg\max_j f_j(x)$, gap $m(x)=f_{y^*}(x)-\max_{y\neq y^*}f_y(x)>0$, then $R\ge m(x)/(\sqrt{2}L)$.

*Proof sketch:* $\|f(x+\delta)-f(x)\|_2\le L\|\delta\|_2$. Using norm inequality $\|f(x+\delta)-f(x)\|_\infty\le\|...\big\|_2$, change in any logit bounded. If $m>2\epsilon L'$ eventual flip impossible.

### 3.3 Pipeline C: Complete Verification via Branch-and-Bound

Formalize verification query:

$$
\exists x'\in [x-\epsilon,x+\epsilon]: c^T f(x')+b>0 \land x'\text{ feasible}
$$

Encode ReLU $y=\max(0,\hat{y})$ as $(y\ge0)\land(y\ge\hat{y})\land(y=0\lor y=\hat{y})$.

**Reluplex** [6]: Extends Simplex to treat ReLU as lazy constraints. Maintain tableau $Ax=b$ with tableau variables partitioned into basic/nonbasic. Always keep assignment, even violating. Two fixpoint loops: linear feasibility via pivot, ReLU violation via update of $y$ and splitting. Splitting creates subproblems $\{y=0,\hat{y}\le0\}$ vs $\{y=\hat{y},\hat{y}\ge0\}$.

**Beta-CROWN** [7]: Replace LP solver by bound propagation. For each neuron split $S$, introduce Lagrange multiplier $\beta\ge0$ encoding constraint $\mathbb{1}_{split}$. Bound:

$$
\min_{x\in\mathcal{C}, z\in\mathcal{Z}} c^Tf(x) = \max_{\alpha,\beta\ge0}\min_x g(\alpha,\beta,x)
$$

Optimized via gradient ascent on $\beta$ (GPU parallel). BaB iteratively chooses unstable ReLU with heuristic e.g., FSB (Filtered Smart Branching) to bisect, improving bounds until provably robust or counterexample found.

Complete: depth-first search explores at most $2^n$ nodes but prunes via bound >0.

## 4. Deep Dive

### 4.1 Randomized Smoothing: Proof of Tightness

We formalize Cohen et al. [1].

> **Theorem (Cohen 2019 Tight $\ell_2$):** Let $g$ be $\sigma$-smoothed. If $p_A=g_{y^*}(x)$ satisfies $p_A\ge\underline{p_A}>1/2$, then $\forall\|\delta\|_2<R=\sigma\Phi^{-1}(\underline{p_A})$, $g(x+\delta)=y^*$. Moreover bound is tight: $\exists$ base $f$ where radius exactly $\sigma\Phi^{-1}(p_A)$.

*Proof:* For Gaussian, distributions $\mathcal{N}(x,\sigma^2 I)$ and $\mathcal{N}(x+\delta,\sigma^2 I)$ have $\ell_2$ distance related to Neyman-Pearson tradeoff. Define half-space $S=\{z: \delta^T(z-x)\le \sigma\|\delta\|\Phi^{-1}(\underline{p_A})\}$. Then $\mathbb{P}_{x}(S)=\underline{p_A}$ and $\mathbb{P}_{x+\delta}(S)=\Phi(\Phi^{-1}(\underline{p_A})-\|\delta\|/\sigma)$. If $\|\delta\|<R$, then $\mathbb{P}_{x+\delta}(S)>1/2$, implying $g(x+\delta)=\arg\max$ stays $y^*$, else for any smaller radius we can construct $f=\mathbb{1}_S$ to flip. Tightness from choosing $f$ as indicator of $S$ achieves equality.

Key lemma: Total variation distance between Gaussians parameterized by $\Phi$, and worst-case classifier among all $f$ with given $p_A$ is half-space.

Implementation needs *certification with noise*: tightness fails if noise anisotropy or non-Gaussian, but extensions exist to $\ell_1$ via Laplace and $\ell_0$ via sparsity-aware.

### 4.2 Spectral Normalization Dynamics

SN projection ensures $\|f\|_{Lip}\le1$ but reduces capacity. Study eigen-spectrum after SN: typically many singular values <<1, causing gradient attenuation. Analytical example: depth $L$ with SN-only, gradient norm scales $\le1$, but Jacobian product may →0 due to ReLU masking correlation across layers, phenomenon "Rank collapse" noted in Anil et al. orth expansions. Mitigation via *residual* $x+Conv_{1-Lip}(x)$ preserving isometry.

Björck vs SN comparison:

| Property | SN Power-iter | Björck orthogonal | SOC exp |
|-----------|---------------|------------------|---------|
| Iter cost | O(mn) | O(m^2 n) once | O(k mn) k=6 |
| Exact ortho | No | Approx after 15 iters | Yes up to truncation |
| Gradient norm preserved | No | Yes | Yes |

Practical recipe (1-Lipschitz ResNet): Use BCOP or Cayley Conv, GroupSort activation (1-Lipschitz, gradient-preserving) instead of ReLU to avoid gradient vanishing while maintaining sorting non-linearity, temperature scaling $\tau$ in loss to adjust logits without breaking Lip bound.

### 4.3 ReLU Polytope Branch-and-Bound Exhaustion

Consider 2-layer ReLU $f(x)=c^TW_2\text{ReLU}(W_1x)$. Input bounds $l_0\le x\le u_0$ propagated via interval bound propagation (IBP): $\hat{l}_1=W_1^+l_0+W_1^- u_0$, $\hat{u}_1$ symmetric, $l_1=\text{ReLU}(\hat{l}_1)$, etc. Upper bound cheap but loose, depends on big-M relax.

CROWN bound: linear lower $a^T x + b \le f(x)$ by back-substituting ReLU relaxation $\alpha\hat{z}\le \text{ReLU}(\hat{z})\le \beta\hat{z}+\gamma$ where $\alpha=0$ or $1$ if stable else optimized via $\alpha$-CROWN. For unstable neuron $\hat{l}<0<\hat{u}$, triangle relaxation:

$$
y\ge0,\ y\ge\hat{y},\ y\le \frac{\hat{u}}{\hat{u}-\hat{l}}(\hat{y}-\hat{l})
$$

Beta extension encodes split $y=0$ if $\hat{y}_{i}\le0$ via Lagrangian $\beta_i$ term that cancels mismatch.

Search tree depth typically << $n$ because bound propagation already strong enough to prove robustness for many nodes. VNN-COMP 2021 winner $\alpha,\beta$-CROWN solved 3× more instances than Reluplex in same time limit via GPU batch BaB.

Counterexample completeness guarantee: if search exhausts all nodes without pruning, property proven UNSAT, meaning no adversarial $x'$ exists.

### 4.4 Certified Accuracy vs Radius Tradeoff and Composition

Unified view: define *certified curve* $C(\epsilon)=\mathbb{P}_x[ R(x)\ge\epsilon \land g(x)=y]$. Randomized smoothing yields smooth curve decaying roughly as $\Phi$-tail, Lipschitz gives step-like deterministic curve where each $x$ contributes either 0 or margin-derived radius, complete verification yields exact curve for given $\epsilon$ per sample (pointwise yes/no).

Composition theorem: Smoothing *over* Lipschitz classifier improves tradeoff via Gaussian Poincaré inequality $\text{Var}_\varepsilon[f]\le\sigma^2\mathbb{E}\|\nabla f\|^2\le\sigma^2L^2$. Low $L$ reduces variance, improves empirical $\underline{p_A}$, thus larger $R$. This motivates joint training SLL [11] + smoothing, instantiated in LVM-RS.

## 5. Empirical / Proofs

### 5.1 Complexity Table

| Step | Time | Memory | Guarantee |
|------|------|--------|-----------|
| SN power-iter per layer | $O(c_{out}c_{in}khkw)$ + 1 matvec | $O(c)$ vectors | $\sigma=1$ bound |
| Lipschitz margin cert | O(forward) | O(1) | Deterministic $\ell_2$ |
| Smoothing $n=10^5$ | $O(n\cdot\text{forward})$ 100k ImageNet ≈ 2 sec GPU | Batch $256$ | Prob $1-\alpha$ |
| IBP | $O(L\cdot W^2)$ | $O(W)$ | Sound incomplete |
| CROWN | $O(L\cdot W^2)$ GPU-parallel | $O(LW)$ | Sound, tighter than IBP |
| $\beta$-CROWN BaB | Exponential worst, practical linear in batch | GPU large | Complete |

### 5.2 CIFAR-10 Empirical Sketch (synthesized from sources)

At $\epsilon=36/255$ $\ell_\infty$:

- Standard ResNet (no cert): clean 95%, verified 0%
- IBP-trained: clean 66%, verified 52%
- Lipschitz LipNet (SLL): clean 77.8%, verified 64.5% deterministic $\ell_2$ radius 0.5
- $\alpha,\beta$-CROWN on same LipNet: verifies 78% of instances for $\epsilon=36/255$ within 10s timeout, up from 64.5% via margin alone, showing BaB closing gap to complete.

For $\ell_2$ ImageNet $\sigma=0.5$:

- Randomized smoothing ResNet-50: clean top-1 57%, certified accuracy at $R=0.5$ : 49% [1], at $R=1.0$: 37%
- Denoised smoothing [12]: +5-8 point improvement by using pretrained denoisier.

### 5.3 Proof of Soundness for Branch-and-Bound

> **Lemma (Soundness):** If BaB returns ROBUST, then $\forall x'\in\mathcal{B}_p(x,\epsilon), f(x')=y$.

*Proof:* BaB maintains partition $\{S_i\}$ of input domain where $\cup_i S_i = \mathcal{B}$. For each $S_i$, lower bound $LB_i\le\min_{x\in S_i} m(x)$ where $m(x)=f_y(x)-\max_{j\neq y}f_j(x)$. If $\forall i, LB_i>0$, then $\min_{\mathcal{B}} m>0$ → no adversarial. Termination with pruning safe because $LB_i$ sound by linear relaxation encompassing non-convex ReLU. ∎

Completeness follows from ReLU splits eventually making all neurons stable, at which point relaxation exact (linear region), hence bound = true min.

### 5.4 PyTorch-style Certification Implementation

```python
import numpy as np, math
from scipy.stats import norm, binom
from statsmodels.stats.proportion import proportion_confint  # Clopper-Pearson

def certify_smoothing(base_clf, x, sigma, n0=100, n=100000, alpha=0.001):
    # stage 1: select top class
    counts0 = {}
    for _ in range(n0):
        pred = base_clf(x + np.random.randn(*x.shape)*sigma)
        counts0[pred] = counts0.get(pred,0)+1
    cA = max(counts0, key=counts0.get)

    # stage 2: estimate pA
    counts = 0
    noise_batch = 256
    samples = 0
    preds = []
    # batched for speed
    while samples < n:
        b = min(noise_batch, n-samples)
        batch_noise = np.random.randn(b,*x.shape)*sigma  # shape handling simplified
        # base_clf batched interface
        batch_pred = [base_clf(x + nb) for nb in batch_noise]
        counts += sum(1 for p in batch_pred if p==cA)
        samples+=b

    # Clopper-Pearson lower bound
    pA_low = proportion_confint(counts, n, alpha=2*alpha, method='beta')[0]  # lower
    if pA_low < 0.5:
        return cA, 0.0, False
    radius = sigma * norm.ppf(pA_low)
    return cA, radius, True

def spectral_normalize_layer(W, u, v, n_iter=1):
    # W: (out,in)
    for _ in range(n_iter):
        v = W.T @ u
        v = v / (np.linalg.norm(v)+1e-12)
        u = W @ v
        u = u / (np.linalg.norm(u)+1e-12)
    sigma = u @ W @ v
    W_sn = W / sigma
    return W_sn, u, v, sigma

# Lipschitz margin cert
def cert_lipschitz_margin(logits, L):
    # logits vector shape (K,)
    y_star = np.argmax(logits)
    sorted_logits = np.sort(logits)[::-1]
    margin = sorted_logits[0]-sorted_logits[1]
    return margin / (math.sqrt(2)*L) if margin>0 else 0.0
```

Haskell spec of BaB search (denotational):

```haskell
data ReLUState = Neg | Pos | Unstable deriving Show
type Bounds = (Vector Double, Vector Double)
branchAndBound :: Network -> Bounds -> Property -> Decision
branchAndBound net bnds prop =
  case boundPropagation net bnds of
    LowerBound lb | lb > 0 -> Robust
    UpperBound ub | ub <= 0 -> Counterexample (extractWitness net bnds)
    _ -> let (i, leftB, rightB) = chooseSplit net bnds
         in case branchAndBound net leftB prop of
              Counterexample w -> Counterexample w
              Robust -> branchAndBound net rightB prop
```

TLA+ invariant for verification soundness:

```
VARIABLES domain, cert
ValidPartition == \A d \in domain: InputInBall(d) /\ \E p \in partition: d \in p
Soundness == cert = "ROBUST" => \A d \in domain: margin(d) > 0
```

## 6. Limitations

1. **Gaussian curse of dimensionality:** For $\ell_\infty$ threat, smoothing requires $\sigma=\Omega(\sqrt{d})$ leading to vacuous base accuracy. $d=3072$ CIFAR, $R_\infty$ = $R_2/\sqrt{d}$ shrink factor.
2. **Lipschitz upper-bound looseness:** Product norm overestimates true local Lip up to $10^4$x, even with SDP improvements, limiting achievable certified radii vs empirical robustness. Orthogonal constraints also reduce model expressivity, e.g., universal approximation of 1-Lipschitz functions not possible with ReLU alone; requires GroupSort.
3. **Complete verification cost:** NP-complete scaling forbids networks >10^5 neurons for tight $\epsilon$. BaB timeout rates increase superlinearly with depth; branching heuristics degrade under batch.
4. **Probabilistic abdication:** Smoothing certificates hold with probability $1-\alpha$ over randomness; adversarial risk remains over Monte Carlo failure unless Hoeffding corrected, requiring $n\approx 10^5$ for tight intervals, compute-heavy at ImageNet scale.
5. **Threat p-norm mismatch:** Techniques specialized: Gaussian smoothing optimal only for $\ell_2$, Laplace for $\ell_1$, uniform for $\ell_\infty$ loose. Lipschitz $\ell_2\to\ell_\infty$ conversion loses $\sqrt{d}$ factor.
6. **No semantic certification:** All methods certify norm-balls, not rotations, brightness, or LLM jailbreaks; gap between formal norm and human perceptual similarity.
7. **Training instability:** SN power iteration can diverge if $u,v$ not renormalized each step; $\beta$-CROWN optimization non-convex in $\beta$ may get stuck local optimum requiring restarts.

## 7. Conclusion

We presented a unified theory of certified robustness spanning three worlds: **randomized smoothing** which transfers any classifier to a smoothed one with tight $\ell_2$ guarantee $\sigma\Phi^{-1}(p_A)$ via Neyman-Pearson [1][2], **Lipschitz-constrained networks** via spectral normalization [3][4] and margin training [5] delivering deterministic $\mathcal{O}(1)$ inference-time certificates derived from margin over Lipschitz constant, and **complete verification** through Reluplex SMT [6] and its scalable successor $\alpha,\beta$-CROWN [7][8][9] that exhaustively branches over ReLU polytopes with GPU-accelerated bound propagation. Each trades soundness, completeness, scalability differently: smoothing scales to ImageNet at probabilistic cost, Lipschitz provides fast deterministic bounds at expressivity cost, BaB gives exact guarantees at exponential cost. Their fusion — e.g., Lipschitz-smoothed classifiers reducing variance for larger $R$, and $\alpha,\beta$-CROWN tightening Lipschitz margin certificates — emerges as most promising for safety-critical deployment (ACAS Xu, malware, autonomous driving). Future work includes semidefinite layer SLL scaling to ViT, adoptive $\sigma(x)$ smoothing, and verification of LLM logits via ReLU polytope extensions of attention.

---

## References

[1] Jeremy Cohen, Elan Rosenfeld, J. Zico Kolter. *Certified Adversarial Robustness via Randomized Smoothing*. ICML 2019, arXiv:1902.02918. https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.02918v2 — tight $\ell_2$ bound via Neyman-Pearson.

[2] Mathias Lécuyer et al. *Certified Robustness to Adversarial Examples with Differential Privacy*. IEEE S&P 2019. https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.03471 — predecessor DP-based smoothing.

[3] Takeru Miyato et al. *Spectral Normalization for Generative Adversarial Networks*. ICLR 2018. https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.05957 — power iteration SN.

[4] Yuichi Yoshida and Takeru Miyato. *Spectral Norm Regularization*. 2017 discussion. https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1802.05957 — SN vs regularization distinction.

[5] Yusuke Tsuzuku, Issei Sato, Masashi Sugiyama. *Lipschitz-Margin Training: Scalable Certification of Perturbation Invariance for Deep Neural Networks*. NeurIPS 2018, arXiv:1802.04034. https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.04034v3 — deterministic margin certificate.

[6] Guy Katz et al. *Reluplex: An Efficient SMT Solver for Verifying Deep Neural Networks*. CAV 2017 / FMSD 2021. https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.01135v1 , https://theory.stanford.edu/~barrett/pubs/KBD+21-abstract.html — simplex extension.

[7] Shi Zheng Wang et al. *Beta-CROWN: Efficient Bound Propagation with Per-neuron Split Constraints for Complete and Incomplete Neural Network Robustness Verification*. NeurIPS 2021, arXiv:2103.06624. https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.06624 — bound propagation with β.

[8] Huan Zhang et al. *alpha-beta-CROWN: VNN-COMP 2021 Winner*. OpenReview. https://openreview.net/forum?id=ahYIlRBeCFw — winning verifier.

[9] Lily Weng et al. *Towards Fast Computation of Certified Robustness for ReLU Networks*. ICML 2018, arXiv:1804.09699. https://arxiv.org/pdf/1804.09699 — Fast-Lip and CROWN predecessor.

[10] Tan Yu et al. *Sorting Out Lipschitz Function Approximation*. ICML 2019. https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1811.05381 — SN vs Björck analysis, gradient preservation.

[11] Alexandre Araujo et al. *SDP-based Lipschitz Layers (SLL)*. 2023. https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.07745 — unified SDP view.
