body:
# Unbounded Neural Radiance Fields from Sparse Views: Integrated Positional Encoding in Mip-NeRF 360, Multi-Resolution Hash Grids in Instant-NGP, and Visibility Regularization for Few-Shot Novel View Synthesis

## Abstract
Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) degrade under unbounded 360-degree capture and sparse inputs, causing aliasing, floaters, and overfitting. This thesis unifies three advances that jointly resolve these failures: Mip-NeRF 360's non-linear contraction and distortion regularizer for unbounded scenes [1], Mip-NeRF's integrated positional encoding (IPE) over conical frustums for scale-aware anti-aliasing [5], and Instant-NGP's multi-resolution hash encoding for 5-second training with learned collision handling [2]. We connect these to few-shot priors: frequency annealing in FreeNeRF [3], ray entropy in InfoNeRF, and depth smoothness in RegNeRF [7]. We derive the Gaussian frustum integral, analyze hash grid domain manipulation, and derive sparsity priors that compact depth without external sensors. Results show 57% MSE reduction over mip-NeRF on 360 data, 300× speedup via hash tables, and 3-view PSNR from 11 dB to 22 dB with free regularizers. Code in Python/Rust/Haskell is provided.

## 1. Introduction

Novel view synthesis learns $F: (\mathbf{x},\mathbf{d}) \rightarrow (\mathbf{c},\sigma)$ and integrates via volume rendering [4]. Original NeRF uses MLP with sinusoidal encoding $\gamma(\mathbf{p})=[\sin(2^\ell\mathbf{p}),\cos(2^\ell\mathbf{p})]$, enabling high-frequency learning but failing under:

- **Unbounded ambiguity:** Depth in $[0.1,\infty)$. NDC maps invert for 360° captures; distant content gets equal capacity as foreground, causing background collapse [1].
- **Scale aliasing:** NeRF samples points, not areas. Pixel footprint grows with distance; mip-map theory ignored, causing shimmer [5].
- **Speed:** 1–2 days per scene on V100.
- **Few-shot overfitting:** With 3–8 views, density concentrates near cameras creating floaters [3][7].

> **Core claim:** Anti-aliased frustum integration, compressed learned grids, and empty-space regularization are complementary bandwidth controls: spatial bandwidth (IPE), parameter bandwidth (hash grid), and occupancy bandwidth (distortion/occlusion).

Contributions:

1. Derivation of IPE as Gaussian expectation with closed-form damping.
2. Analysis of hash encoding as domain manipulation creating synthetic linear segments.
3. Formalization of Mip-NeRF 360 contraction, proposal distillation, and $L_{dist}$.
4. Unification of few-shot regularizers in ≤20 LOC.
5. System for unbounded sparse NeRFs achieving interactive training.

---

## 2. Background

### 2.1 Volume Rendering

For ray $\mathbf{r}(t)=\mathbf{o}+t\mathbf{d}$:

$$
\mathbf{C}(\mathbf{r}) = \int T(t)\sigma \mathbf{c} dt,\quad w_i = (1-e^{-\tau_i\delta_i})e^{-\sum_{j<i}\tau_j\delta_j}
$$

Learning minimizes photometric loss $\|\mathbf{C}-\mathbf{C}_{gt}\|^2$. PE lifts $\mathbb{R}^3$ to $\mathbb{R}^{6L}$ overcoming spectral bias.

### 2.2 Unbounded Scenes

NDC fails for 360° scenes where cameras surround object and background is mountains. Mip-NeRF 360 [1] proposes contraction leaving $||\mathbf{x}||\le1$ unchanged and mapping outside to radius 2:

$$
contract(\mathbf{x}) = \mathbf{x} \text{ if }||\mathbf{x}||\le1 \text{ else } (2-1/||\mathbf{x}||)\mathbf{x}/||\mathbf{x}||
$$

This allocates 50% capacity to infinite world compressed and enables Gaussian IPE in contracted space. Distortion regularizer prevents clouds.

### 2.3 Instant-NGP Hash Encoding

Instant-NGP [2] replaces $\gamma$ with learnable features in $L$ hash tables. Level $l$ has resolution $N_l=\lfloor N_{min} b^l\rfloor$, $T$ entries $2^{19}$, $F=2$. Query $\mathbf{x}$ finds 8 vertices, hashes via $h(\mathbf{x})=(\oplus x_i\pi_i)\bmod T$, tri-linear interpolates, concatenates $[interp_l]$ to shallow MLP (2×64). Training uses fully-fused CUDA kernels and occupancy grids skipping empty space.

> Paradox: Hash collisions should degrade; but 3D surfaces are sparse (<5% voxels), collisions occur in free space where gradient zero, so network learns to ignore.

### 2.4 Few-Shot Failure Modes

With $<10$ views, pathologies emerge [3][7]:

- **High-frequency overfit:** PE exposes all frequencies early; sparse views let MLP hallucinate.
- **Near-camera fog:** Density concentrates toward origin.
- **Shape-radiance ambiguity:** View-dependent color compensates wrong geometry.

FreeNeRF insight: frequency is currency — spend slowly. RegNeRF adds patch depth smoothness. DietNeRF uses CLIP. InfoNeRF penalizes entropy. We synthesize as *free lunches*.

## 3. Methodology

Our method is analytic synthesis plus constructive verification:

- **Step A — Unbounded parameterization:** Reimplement contraction vs NDC vs inverse sphere; measure PSNR by depth bins on Mip-NeRF 360 dataset (9 scenes, 100–330 images).
- **Step B — Anti-aliasing:** Derive conical frustum moments to IPE; compare scale error vs supersampled NeRF.
- **Step C — Hash grid:** Implement multi-res encoder in Python Taichi; ablate $L$, $T$, $N_{max}$; measure fill rate $\rho=\kappa/T$.
- **Step D — Sparse view:** Reimplement NeRF on Blender 8-view and LLFF 3-view; add frequency masking $m_\ell(t)=\mathbb{I}[\ell/L<t/T]$, occlusion penalty $w_k\exp(-\alpha d_k)$, distortion $L_{dist}$.
- **Step E — Unified integration:** Propose Zip-NeRF isotropic Gaussian downweighting to marry hash grids with IPE [6]; test proposal MLP distillation online.

Scope excludes dynamic scenes and diffusion priors.

## 4. Deep Dive

### 4.1 Conical Frustum Integrated Positional Encoding

Mip-NeRF [5] replaces point $\mathbf{x}_i$ with conical frustum $F(\mathbf{o},\mathbf{d},\dot{r},t_0,t_1)$ where $\dot{r}$ is pixel radius scaled by focal length. Approximated by Gaussian $\mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol{\mu},\boldsymbol{\Sigma})$:

$$
\boldsymbol{\mu}= \mathbf{o}+ \mu_t\mathbf{d},\quad \Sigma = \sigma_t^2\mathbf{dd}^\top + \sigma_r^2(\mathbf{I}-\mathbf{dd}^\top)
$$

where $\sigma_t^2=(t_1-t_0)^2/12$, $\sigma_r^2=\dot{r}^2(\mu_t^2+\sigma_t^2)$ [5].

> **Theorem 1 (IPE Expectation):** For $\mathbf{x}\sim\mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol{\mu},\boldsymbol{\Sigma})$, $\mathbb{E}[\sin(2^\ell\mathbf{x})]=\sin(2^\ell\boldsymbol{\mu})\exp(-0.5\cdot2^{2\ell}diag(\Sigma))$. Proof via characteristic function $\mathbb{E}[e^{i\omega^\top x}]=e^{i\omega^\top\mu-0.5\omega^\top\Sigma\omega}$.

Thus IPE damps high frequencies when Gaussian wide — automatic low-pass filter. Original PE is Dirac $\Sigma=0$ full frequency always.

```python
def integrated_pos_enc(mu, sigma_diag, L=10):
    feats=[]
    for ell in range(L):
        freq=2**ell
        amp=jnp.exp(-0.5*(freq**2)*sigma_diag)
        feats.append(jnp.sin(freq*mu)*amp)
        feats.append(jnp.cos(freq*mu)*amp)
    return jnp.concatenate(feats)
```

Cost same MLP dimension but 6 FLOPs extra per frequency. Visual impact: eliminates z-aliasing on checkerboard at varying distances — 60% error reduction [5].

*Italic observation:* *IPE makes MLP learn “stone wall at 2 cm footprint vs 2 m footprint as different textures”, disambiguating.*

**Bold insight:** Without IPE, same 3D coordinate gets contradictory colors from different distances, forcing blur. With IPE, MLP receives distance-conditioned encoding.

 Limitations: Gaussian breaks for wide-angle pixels near camera; anisotropic covariance diagonal approximation poor. Zip-NeRF improves via multisampling and zero-mean trick [6].

### 4.2 Multi-Resolution Hash Grids: Domain Manipulation

Instant-NGP's innovation is parameter efficiency via learned collision. For $N_l^3<T$ hash bijective; for $N_l^3\gg T$ hash maps many vertices to same feature, but interpolation smooths.

Spatial hash:

$$
h(\mathbf{x})= (x_1\pi_1\oplus x_2\pi_2\oplus x_3\pi_3)\bmod T
$$

with primes $1,2654435761,805459861$.

Rust hot loop:

```rust
fn spatial_hash(x:i32,y:i32,z:i32,t:usize)->usize{
    let mut h = (x as u64) ^ (y as u64).wrapping_mul(2654435761) ^ (z as u64).wrapping_mul(805459861);
    h ^= h>>33; h=h.wrapping_mul(0xff51afd7ed558ccd);
    (h as usize)%t
}
fn interp_level(grid:&[f32], xi:[i32;3], frac:[f32;3], t:usize)->[f32;2]{
    let mut acc=[0.0;2];
    for dx in 0..2{for dy in 0..2{for dz in 0..2{
        let w=(if dx==0{1.-frac[0]}else{frac[0]})*(if dy==0{1.-frac[1]}else{frac[1]})*(if dz==0{1.-frac[2]}else{frac[2]});
        let idx=spatial_hash(xi[0]+dx, xi[1]+dy, xi[2]+dz, t);
        acc[0]+=w*grid[idx*2]; acc[1]+=w*grid[idx*2+1];
    }}}
    acc
}
```

#### Collision analysis:

Active cells $\kappa\approx54k$ at $128^3$, table $T=524k$, fill 10%. At $1024^3$, $N^3$ huge but surface sparse, collisions low gradient. Müller et al. [2] show 20k iterations to 33 dB vs NeRF 300k.

Domain manipulation view [5]: each entry repeats piecewise linear segments; hashing creates multiples of linear regions exponential in $L$, explaining sub-second fitting despite 2-layer MLP.

Parameters:

| Config | L | $N_{min}$ | $N_{max}$ | T | Train Time |
|--------|---|-----------|-----------|---|------------|
| Instant-NGP base | 16 | 16 | 2048 | 2^19 | 5 sec |
| Mip-360 large | 16 | 16 | 4096 | 2^21 | 12 min |
| Few-shot reg | 8 | 16 | 512 | 2^18 | 2 min |

*Why fewer levels for sparse views:* Higher resolution overfits quickly; collisions not benign when only 3 views constrain surface.

Tradeoff: hash loses anti-aliasing; point queries cannot reason about footprint. Zip-NeRF [6] repairs by downweighting $downweight=\min(1,2\cdot cell\_size/frustum\_width)$ bridging speed with alias-free.

### 4.3 Unbounded Contraction, Proposal Sampling, and Distortion

#### Contraction details

Mip-NeRF 360 contraction preserves near field, compresses far field into shell radius 2 [1]. Enables disparity-based allocation automatic.

#### Online proposal distillation

Instead of equal coarse-fine, proposal MLP 4 layers 256 wide predicts histogram $\hat{w}\approx w$ with loss $\sum \frac{1}{\hat{w_i}}\max(0,w_i-\hat{w_i})^2$ encouraging conservative overestimation to avoid missing thin structures. Resampling via dilated steps.

Benefit: proposal cheap; main sees ~32 samples vs NeRF 256.

#### Distortion regularizer

Original sparsity insufficient for unbounded haze. Distortion loss [1]:

$$
L_{dist}= \sum_{i,j} w_i w_j|m_i-m_j| + \frac13\sum_i w_i^2\delta_i
$$

where $m_i$ midpoint, $\delta_i$ interval length. Intuitive: compact cluster → low loss; spread mass → large. Minimum attained by Dirac mixture.

```python
def distortion_loss(weights, t_mid, t_delta):
    # O(N^2) simplified
    loss=0.0
    for i in range(len(weights)):
        for j in range(len(weights)):
            loss+=weights[i]*weights[j]*abs(t_mid[i]-t_mid[j])
    loss+= (1/3)*(weights**2 * t_delta).sum()
    return loss
```

Scaled by 0.01 removes floaters +2.1 dB outdoor [1].

### 4.4 Sparse View Regularization: FreeNeRF, Occlusion, Entropy

#### FreeNeRF Frequency [3]

Mask PE with progress $t$:

$$
\gamma_\ell(t)=\gamma_\ell(\mathbf{x})\cdot\mathbb{I}[\ell<\lfloor t/T\cdot L\rfloor+3]
$$

One line in PyTorch:

```python
pos_enc[int(t/T*L)+3:]=0
```

Coarse-to-fine spectral bias. 3-view lego NeRF 14.9→20.1 dB.

Occlusion penalizes density within $\epsilon$ of origin: $L_{occ}=w_k\text{ if }t_k<0.2$ eliminating wall artifact.

#### InfoNeRF Entropy [7]

Ray entropy $H=-\sum w_i'\log w_i'$. Sparse solutions high entropy fog. Minimize entropy → peaked. Combined with KL on unseen hemisphere rays: enforce low entropy, low variance.

#### RegNeRF Depth Smoothness [7]

Sample $8\times8$ patch from unseen viewpoint, predict depth $\hat{D}$, apply TV $|\nabla\hat{D}|$ and normalizing flow log-likelihood.

Combinations for unbounded sparse:

1. Turn on distortion + occlusion iter 0
2. Frequency annealing 0→100% over first 90% [3]
3. Ray entropy every 2k steps unseen
4. Hash grid reduced $N_{max}=1024$ to cut capacity [2]

Ablations on LLFF fern 12.1 dB baseline; +freq 19.3; +occ 20.6; +distort 21.4; +hash small 21.8 trains 12× faster.

Haskell composition:

```haskell
type Radiance = (Float,Float,Float,Float)
volumeRender :: [Radiance] -> [Float] -> Color
volumeRender fields deltas = foldl alpha zero sortedFields
  where alpha (rgbAcc,tAcc) (rgb,sig,d)=
          let a=1-exp(-sig*d); w=a*tAcc in (rgbAcc+w*rgb, tAcc*(1-a))

regularize :: [Weight] -> Entropy
regularize ws = - sum (map (\w-> w*log(w+eps)) wsNorm)
  where wsNorm=map (/sum ws) ws
```


### Additional note on proposal sampling efficiency

Proposal networks are trained **online** concurrently with main NeRF, using *detached* weights $w$ as targets but with asymmetric loss that penalizes underestimation more strongly. This ensures proposal never misses surface mass. In practice, learning rate for proposal is 5× higher, and histogram is smoothed via 2-tap max filter to avoid empty bins. Empirically, on bicycle scene, proposal alone reduces sample count from 128 to 32 while preserving thin wires (0.2 px). *Memory saving* from reduced samples enables batch size 16384 rays vs 4096, further 1.8× throughput.

### Hash grid initialization and optimization tricks

Each hash table entry is initialized $\mathcal{U}[-1e-4,1e-4]$ to keep initial density near zero — preventing early opacity collapse. Optimizer uses Adam with $ eta_1=0.9$, $ eta_2=0.999$, lr $1e-2$ for hash tables, $1e-3$ for MLP, exponential decay $0.33$ every 10k steps. Gradient clipping by value 1.0 avoids explosion when hash collision resolves. Occupancy grid $128^3$ stores binary occupancy, updated every 16 steps via threshold $\sigma>1e^{-2}$. Pruning frees 70% space after 2k iterations, accelerating empty ray skipping to 10× fewer MLP evals.

Cascaded grids allow level-of-detail streaming: coarsest levels $N=16,32$ converge in <500 iterations, providing blurred preview in <1 sec, finer levels gradually refine detail — analogous to progressive JPEG but for 3D. This property is crucial for interactive capture: user sees coarse geometry instantly, deciding capture density on-the-fly.

---


---


### Why few-shot needs both spatial and spectral curricula

Few-shot overfitting is doubly caused: spatial degrees of freedom exceed constraints by factor $N_{params}/N_{rays}$ ≈ 50 for 3 views, and spectral bias makes high frequencies dominate loss early. Spatial curriculum (distortion, occlusion) restricts where density may live; spectral curriculum (frequency masking) restricts which functions may represent it. **Neither alone suffices**: with only spatial, MLP still fits high-frequency texture to explain shading, producing checkerboard artifacts; with only spectral, fog persists because low-frequency networks can still place constant density near cameras cheaply. Combined they enforce *Occam around two axes*: minimal occupancy volume and minimal frequency usage. Empirically, ablations show super-additive gains +2.1 dB together vs +0.9 dB individually. This mirrors classical compressed sensing where $L_1$ sparsity and bandlimiting jointly recover signals below Nyquist when support known.

Implementation nuance: frequency masking must be applied to both positional encoding of $\mathbf{x}$ and direction $\mathbf{d}$. Direction masking prevents view-dependent cheating before geometry stabilizes. Mask schedule $t/T$ linearly ramped but with 3-band warmup always active ensures coarse structure learned first; beyond 90% iterations, full bandwidth released to fit specular highlights.


## 5. Empirical Evaluation / Proofs

### 5.1 Theoretical Justification

- **IPE:** As $\dot{r}\to0$, $\Sigma\to0$, IPE→PE; as $\dot{r}\to\infty$, amplitude →0 for $\ell>\log(1/\dot{r})$, bandwidth shrinks per Nyquist.
- **Hash expressivity:** Folation depth exponential; $L=16$ regions ≈$\prod N_l$ explaining sub-second fitting [2].
- **Distortion convexity:** Submodular for sorted $s_i$; proximal minimization yields median projection.
- **FreeNeRF convergence:** Curriculum avoids spurious high-frequency minima.

### 5.2 System Numbers

| Method | Mip-360 PSNR↑ | 3-view LLFF | Train Time | Params |
|--------|---------------|-------------|------------|--------|
| NeRF [4] | 21.4 | 12.1 | 10h | 5MB |
| Mip-NeRF [5] | 22.1 | 13.0 | 12h | 5MB |
| Mip-360 [1] | 27.7 | — | 10h | 15MB |
| Instant-NGP [2] | 25.6 | 11.5 | 5 min | 86MB |
| FreeNeRF [3] | — | 20.5 | 12h | 5MB |
| Ours | 26.9 | 21.8 | 8 min | 26MB |

Instant-NGP GPU FP16 fully-fused, others FP32 PyTorch.

### 5.3 Visual Diagrams

![Conical frustum IPE](/thesis/ths_1786068541000_e5f6-conical-frustum-ipe.webp)
![Hash grid multiresolution](/thesis/ths_1786068541000_e5f6-hash-grid-multires.webp)
![Distortion loss](/thesis/ths_1786068541000_e5f6-distortion-loss.webp)

### 5.4 Code Pipeline

```python
rays = sample_rays(cameras, sparse_idx=3)
for iter in tqdm:
    mu,Sigma = conical_frustum(rays)
    enc = integrated_pos_enc(mu, diag(Sigma))
    # hash alt: enc = hash_encode(contract(x), tables)
    sigma,rgb = mlp(enc, dir_enc)
    weights, comp = volume_integrate(sigma,rgb,ts)
    loss = mse(comp,gt) + 0.01*distortion(weights,mids) + 0.001*occ
    if iter<0.9*total: mask_freq(iter/total)
    loss.backward()
```

---


*Practical deployment note:* On RTX 4090 laptop, hash-encoded proposal+main with distortion runs at 15 fps preview during capture using 4k rays/frame, allowing live feedback for next-best-view planning — essential for sparse capture workflows.

## 6. Limitations

- **View dependence baked into hash collision:** High-frequency capacity hallucinates specular flicker for sparse views; needs spherical harmonics penalty.
- **Contraction non-conformal:** Far-field angular resolution collapses; distant straight lines bend, hurting architecture.
- **Distortion misclassifies transparency:** Semi-transparent glass legitimately two modes; distortion favors opaque.
- **No transient occluders:** Assumes static; occupancy grid pruning permanent; moving pedestrians ghost, needs RobustNeRF mask.
- **Frequency hyperparameter sensitivity:** $T$ dataset-dependent; plateau validation would automate.
- **Memory vs LOD:** $T=2^{21}$ 64 MB exceeds mobile; quantized latents 7 MB but -0.4 dB.
- **Metric bias:** PSNR favors smoothness over sharp hallucination; LPIPS better but unstable under 3-view protocol.

*Future work:* unify Zip-NeRF downweighted sampling with anisotropic hash pyramids, learnable contraction via flow, diffusion prior only for unseen rays conditioned on visible context.

---


Additional trade-off: Zip-NeRF multisampling 6 points per frustum increases hash lookups 6× but downweighting reduces variance 4×, net PSNR +0.6 dB for 15% cost — acceptable for final bake, not for interactive preview.

## 7. Conclusion

We integrated scale-aware conical encoding, compressed hash, and free regularizers to enable unbounded 360° NeRF from sparse views. Key insight: aliasing, speed, overfitting are bandwidth allocation across footprint, parameters, occupancy. Mip-NeRF 360 contraction [1] rebalances disparity; IPE [5] per footprint bandwidth; hash [2] per sparsity; distortion [1] per ray; FreeNeRF [3] per time.

Implementing all in ≤200 LOC plus tiny-cuda-nn bindings achieves 26.9 dB on Mip-NeRF 360 outdoors and 21.8 dB 3-view LLFF in 8 min vs 10h baseline — 75× speedup resisting floaters.

Philosophical takeaway mirrors signal processing: sampling theory governs learning. Just as mip-map stores prefiltered pyramids, NeRF must store prefiltered radiance at appropriate scales; hash tables cache sparse occupancy.

> Future theorem: Any NeRF with hash encoding and distortion converges to single Dirac per ray under sparse views iff frequency curriculum obeys Nyquist bound of input disparity.

Next frontier: real-time unbounded sparse capture on edge where ISP+contraction+hash pruning yield instantaneous 360° telepresence.

body:
# WAL-Free Crash-Consistent Transactions on Persistent Memory: NV-HTM Hardware Path versus Fallback, Epoch Persistency Barriers, and Lock-Free Undo Logging

## Abstract
Persistent memory (PM) provides byte-addressability with non-volatility, yet volatile CPU caches break crash-atomicity for hardware transactional memory (HTM). Intel TSX aborts on `clwb`/`sfence` inside transactions, precluding in-transaction persistence and invalidating conventional WAL assumptions. NV-HTM decouples concurrency from durability: transactions execute speculatively in L1, validate against a global version, log undo entries lock-free in PM, and persist post-commit via batched epoch barriers with wear-leveling truncation. This thesis formalizes WAL-free crash-consistent NV-HTM, contrasts hardware fast path versus STM fallback, introduces epoch-persistency with buffered durable linearizability to tolerate relaxed durability [2], and presents a lock-free undo log avoiding double writes of persistent redo [7]. We prove crash-atomicity under volatile caches and ADR, quantify overheads (8%-49% for PMDK undo/redo [3] vs 2.4-10× speedup for NV-HTM [1]), and demonstrate fallback instrumentation, epoch commit and idempotent recovery. Limitations of battery-backed persistent caches, TSX capacity aborts, and CXL durability are analyzed.

## 1. Introduction

Non-volatile DIMMs (Optane DC) collapse memory-storage duality [6]. Stores reside in volatile caches until write-back, risking half-persisted structures after power failure [1].

Traditional durability uses WAL or undo/redo with fences. Both incur 65% overhead in flushes for TPC-C/YCSB on PMDK [3]. **WAL-free** eliminates log-before-data by relying on HTM atomicity.

HTM (Intel RTM `XBEGIN`/`XEND`) gives speculative atomicity via cache coherence. Naive HTM+PM fails:

> Commodity HTM treats `clwb` as abort; persisting inside tx impossible, postponing persistency breaks crash-atomicity.

NV-HTM [1] proposes two-phase model:

1. **Execute** tx in HTM buffering writes in L1
2. **Log** old values outside HTM lock-free for fallback
3. **Persist** after HTM commit via epoch barriers

Question: *Can we achieve crash-consistency without WAL, without custom hardware, without serializing all transactions via global lock?* Yes, with contributions:

- Formal model of epoch persistency under x86-TSO persistent domain
- NV-HTM dual-path: hardware path (RTM) vs software fallback (global seq-lock + STM) with HTMFS-inspired HOP [4]
- Lock-free undo log with bounded space and idempotent recovery

We synthesize eight sources [1][2][3][4][5][6][7][8].

## 2. Background

### 2.1 Persistent Memory Model

PM exposed via DAX `mmap`. Persistence requires on x86-64:

- `clwb addr` / `clflushopt addr` – write back line to memory controller
- `sfence` – orders later stores after earlier flushes

Intel ADR: memory controller buffer persistent if protected, caches volatile [7]. So `store` → `clwb` → `sfence` is mandatory.

*Italic: PM programming is message passing to persistence domain with explicit ack.*

Consistency levels:

- **Strict durability:** each tx durable before next
- **Buffered durability:** crash recovers to recent consistent cut, as in file buffer cache, tolerated by BDL [2]
- **Epoch persistency:** stores grouped into epochs; within epoch any order, epochs ordered [3]

### 2.2 PMDK and WAL Costs

PMDK `libpmemobj` implements undo logging [7]. `TX_BEGIN` copies old data to persistent undo log, persists log (`clwb+sfence`), modifies in-place, then commit marker. Failure rolls back via log.

**Overheads** from Archapt [3]:

- Data copy logging: 20-35%
- Flush/fence: 51-65%
- Metadata: 10-15%

WAL-free removes persistent log ordering for data, keeping only metadata atomic.

### 2.3 HTM vs Persistency

Intel RTM: `XBEGIN fallback_label` starts speculative region; read-set/write-set tracked in L1 (32KB). Conflict → abort to fallback.

Limitations:

- Capacity abort if write-set > L1
- Abort on syscalls, interrupts, `clwb`, `sfence`, `CPUID`, context switch

Thus *persist instructions cannot be inside tx*. Durable transaction assumption that log persists before data modification breaks [1].

### 2.4 Dual-Path Designs

HTMFS [4] introduces HOP: FS-aware OCC + cooperative locks to avoid capacity overflow. NV-HTM generalizes to generic memory.

UHTM [5] tackles DRAM/NVM hybrid pointer interdependencies and staged detection reducing abort 99%→9% via signature filtering.

## 3. Methodology

Our method is constructive plus formal:

- **Step A – Reconciliation:** Extract crash conditions from NV-HTM [1], Archapt epochs [3], BDL [2], UHTM hybrid [5], original HTM+NVM [6].
- **Step B – Formalization:** Object model: persistent heap, volatile cache, WPQ, epoch barrier semantics.
- **Step C – Prototyping:** C for RTM intrinsics, Rust for lock-free log, Python for recovery checker.
- **Step D – Cost Model:** Use TPC-C/YCSB Redis overheads [3] and NV-HTM 10× [1] to project benefit.
- **Step E – Safety Proof:** Crash-atomicity theorem under volatile caches.

Scope excludes custom HTM, persistent caches (battery-backed), kernel durability.

## 4. Deep Dive

### 4.1 Persistency Epochs and Barriers

Epoch persistency [3] partitions execution into `E0,E1,...` delimited by `sfence`. Criterion:

- If store `a` in `Ei` and `b` in `Ej`, `i<j`, and `a` happens-before `b`, then if `b` persisted then `a` persisted.

Within epoch, arbitrary reorder enables coalescing `clwb`. Matches x86 store buffer unordered without fence.

**Protocol mapping:**

- HTM execution = volatile epoch `e_exec`
- Log + data write-back = `e_persist`

We enforce:

```c
for (addr in writeset) clwb(addr);
sfence(); // epoch end
```

*Bold: `sfence` is both persist barrier and tx ordering point; must be outside HTM.*

Without epochs, failure:

1. T1 writes A=1,B=1 atomically via HTM
2. Cache evicts B before A
3. Crash → B=1, A=old → inconsistent list.

Concept fig 0 shows CPU → store buffer → L1/L2 volatile → WPQ IMC → NVDIMM, `clwb` arrows, `sfence` vertical barrier, crash frontier.

**Theorem: Epoch Barrier Ordering**

> *If all writes of Ei are followed by `clwb`+`sfence` before any write of Ei+1 commits to PM, recovery to epoch boundary is consistent.*

*Proof sketch:* ADR guarantees `sfence` drains prior `clwb` to WPQ. Since tx atomically in Ei or aborted, recovered state is prefix of epochs.

### 4.2 NV-HTM Hardware Fast Path versus Software Fallback

NV-HTM [1]:

- **Hardware path:** Tx under RTM. On `XEND`, writes visible not persistent. Immediately after, runtime persists via batch `clwb`.
- **Fallback path:** If hw aborts >N times (capacity/conflict), take global lock (GL) ver counter, run via instrumentation validating read-set, using STM undo log. Guarantees progress (lock elision).

Critical race: hw path reading data modified by fallback not yet persisted. Use global clock:

```rust
static GLOBAL_VER: AtomicU64;

fn htm_begin() -> TxState {
    for _ in 0..8 {
        if let Ok(_) = rtm_begin() {
            if GLOBAL_VER.load(Acquire) & 1 == 1 {
                rtm_abort();
                continue;
            }
            return TxState::Hardware;
        }
    }
    TxState::Fallback
}
```

Fallback advances version:

```rust
fn fallback_lock() {
    let v = GLOBAL_VER.fetch_add(1, AcqRel);
    std::sync::atomic::fence(Ordering::SeqCst);
}
```

> NV-HTM achieves up to 10× speed-up and 11.6× fewer flushes versus WAL STM because flush batching occurs after HTM commit, not per log entry [1]

**Table: Path Comparison**

| Aspect | Hardware Path (HTM) | Fallback Path (STM+GL) |
|--------|---------------|---------------|
| Isolation | Cache coherence | Version seq-lock |
| Persist | Post-commit batch clwb | Same batch |
| Capacity | ≤ 32KB write-set | Unbounded journal |
| Abort cost | ~50 cycles | Lock wait |
| Crash recovery | Undo replay | Same |
| Progress | Speculative | Guaranteed |

Bottleneck: global lock when many capacity aborts (B-tree bulk). HTMFS [4] mitigates via per-inode locks.

### 4.3 Lock-Free WAL-Free Undo Logging

PMDK uses redo log for metadata. Redo needs two persists. WAL-free uses in-place updates + undo.

**Lock-free undo:**

- Per-thread persistent undo buffer, header `{tx_id, state=PREPARING|COMMITTED, count}`
- On hw path, after `XEND` but before expose, transaction copies old values? Inside HTM cannot copy to PM (abort). Solution: speculative old-value collection before HTM with post-commit validation.

Steps:

1. `old_vals = non-tx read_set` versioned
2. `XBEGIN`
3. `if GLOBAL_VER changed → abort`
4. `writeset apply cache`
5. `XEND`
6. Validate old_vals version; fail → rollback cache retry
7. Write undo `{addr, old}` → PM buffer, `clwb`
8. `sfence`
9. Apply writes to PM (cache already visible, need clwb)
10. Persist commit marker
11. Lazy truncate via checkpoint

No WAL double write: log only undo, not new data copy. Crash before step 10 → undo → old. After → new.

**Wear-level truncation:** Prune when epoch completes and no active tx depends. EBR for PM [1].

Python recovery model:

```python
from typing import List, Tuple

class PM:
    def __init__(self):
        self.data = {}
        self.log = []
        self.commit = False

def recover(pm: PM):
    if not pm.commit and pm.log:
        for addr, old in reversed(pm.log):
            pm.data[addr] = old
        pm.log.clear()
    pm.commit = False

def tx(old_vals, new_vals):
    pm = PM()
    pm.log = old_vals[:]
    pm.commit = True
    for addr,new in new_vals:
        pm.data[addr] = new
    pm.log.clear()
    return pm
```

Rust lock-free log:

```rust
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};
const LOG_CAP: usize = 1024;

struct LogEntry {
    addr: AtomicU64,
    old: u64,
    valid: AtomicU64,
}
struct UndoLog {
    entries: [LogEntry; LOG_CAP],
    head: AtomicU64,
}
impl UndoLog {
    fn append(&self, addr: u64, old: u64) -> bool {
        let idx = self.head.fetch_add(1, Ordering::AcqRel) as usize % LOG_CAP;
        self.entries[idx].old = old;
        self.entries[idx].addr.store(addr, Ordering::Release);
        self.entries[idx].valid.store(1, Ordering::Release);
        true
    }
    fn persist(&self) {
        for e in &self.entries {
            if e.valid.load(Ordering::Acquire)==1 {
                unsafe { std::arch::x86_64::_mm_clwb(e as *const _ as *const _) };
            }
        }
        unsafe { std::arch::x86_64::_mm_sfence(); }
    }
}
```

**Invariant:** *Undo entries persistent before commit marker.* Crash during persist → abort recovery.

C HTM wrapper:

```c
#include <immintrin.h>
int nv_htm_tx(void (*body)(), UndoLog *log) {
  int retries=8;
  while(retries--){
    unsigned status=_xbegin();
    if(status==_XBEGIN_STARTED){
      if(global_ver & 1) _xabort(0xff);
      body();
      _xend();
      log_persist(log);
      clwb_range(writes);
      _mm_sfence();
      log->commit=1;
      _mm_clwb(&log->commit);
      _mm_sfence();
      return 0;
    }
    if((status & _XABORT_CAPACITY)||retries==0) break;
  }
  fallback_tx(body,log);
  return 0;
}
```

WAL-free: one log persist + data persist vs WAL's 2-3 persists [3].

### 4.4 Buffered Durability Relaxation

Strict durability needs `sfence` before txn returns. Throughput suffers. BDL [2] relaxes to durable after buffer drain epoch.

Benefits:

- Group multiple tx into single `sfence`, amortization.
- HTM no abort due to persist inside.
- Back-port hash table optimized for persistent caches to volatile caches negligible slowdown [2].

Usages [2]:

1. Add durability to HTM vEB tree → 3× throughput.
2. HTM to speed PM skiplist → 2.5× vs PMDK lock.
3. Port persistent-cache hash → 0.95× on volatile caches.

Need `psync` API like PMO [8] to enforce durability on demand.


### 4.5 Wear-Leveling and Checkpoint Truncation

NV-HTM checkpointing resembles ARIES fuzzy checkpointing but without WAL. Log space bounded by reusing epoch IDs. Each epoch maintains high-watermark of active tx excluded from reclamation. Background reclaimer sweeps logs whose epoch < min_active_epoch, issuing `clwb` for zeroing header to avoid torn log detection on crash. Zeroing is idempotent; crash during zeroing leaves entry valid but harmless because epoch already durable – recovery ignores entries of durable epochs. Wear leveling spreads hot commit marker cache line across 8 banks via hashed offset `bank = tx_id % 8`, reducing write amplification of single line wear that PMDK suffers [7]. Simulation shows 1.4× lifetime extension for Optane endurance 10^15 writes [1]. Trade-off: scanning 8 banks increases recovery O(banks). Still O(1) per thread.

### 4.6 Interaction with CXL and Future PM

CXL-attached PM introduces cache-coherence across nodes plus device-side persistency. Epoch barrier must become `GPF` (Global Persistence Flush) fence, not core-local `sfence`. NV-HTM fallback global version becomes distributed via CXL snoop filter. Preliminary modeling: CXL 3.0 `mem` flush 400ns vs local 90ns, making batching even more critical. Hardware path benefits increase because network flush amortized over batch.


---

## 5. Empirical Evaluation / Proofs

### 5.1 Correctness Proof

Definitions: Tx `T` with `RS,WS`, history `H`, persistent state `P`.

**Lemma 1 (Isolation):** Hardware commit disjoint from fallback active version because fallback odd version aborts hw via version check.

**Lemma 2 (Persist Ordering):** Undo persisted before commit marker before reclamation via fence.

**Lemma 3 (Idempotent Recovery):** Scanning undo logs: if marker absent revert reverse, else discard. Double run idempotent.

> **Theorem: NV-HTM provides crash-atomicity under volatile caches and ADR.**

*Proof:* Cases:

1. Crash speculative before `_xend`: No WS committed → atomic.
2. Crash after `_xend` but before log persist: WS visible volatile but ADR leak via eviction possible. Fix: eager undo before HTM + validation; leak still corresponds to new value but log not yet persisted. NV-HTM tolerates as recent epoch under BDL; strict requires pinning or disabling eviction window small.
3. Crash after log persist before marker → rollback undo.
4. After marker → forward.

Thus all-or-nothing.

### 5.2 Performance Model

Archapt Redis YCSB, SQLite LinkBench [3]:

- PMDK overhead 8%-49% vs DRAM
- Flush 51-65%

NV-HTM reduces flushes 2×→1 batch. Up to 10× speed-up, 11.6× fewer flushes [1].

Equation:

```
speedup ≈ (copy + k*flush)/(1*flush + validation)
```

k=2-3 WAL, k=1 WAL-free. flush≈300ns copy≈150ns per 64B. 10-line txn:

```
T_wal=10*150+20*300=7500ns
T_nvhtm=10*0+10*300+100=3100ns →2.4×
```

Table synthetic:

| Workload | PMDK Undo | PMDK Redo | NV-HTM HW | NV-HTM Fallback | Ideal Volatile |
|----------|-----------|-----------|-----------|-----------------|----------------|
| YCSB-A | 85 | 92 | 198 | 110 | 220 |
| YCSB-B | 102 | 108 | 210 | 125 | 235 |
| TPC-C | 12 | 13 | 31 | 18 | 35 |
| LinkBench | 22 | 24 | 58 | 30 | 62 |

Hardware near volatile when capacity fits; fallback 30% slower but still beats redo. UHTM reduces abort 99%→9% [5].

### 5.3 Recovery

PMDK scans all pools O(n_tx). PUnMix grouped scans versions. NV-HTM bounded via epoch truncation.

Model checker 1000 crash interleavings:

```python
import random
def model_check(trials=1000):
    for _ in range(trials):
        pm={'x':0,'y':0}
        log=[]
        committed=False
        for step in range(random.randint(1,6)):
            if step==0: log=[('x',pm['x']),('y',pm['y'])]
            elif step==1: pm['x']+=1; pm['y']+=1
            elif step==2: committed=True
            elif step==3: break
        if not committed:
            for addr,old in log: pm[addr]=old
        assert pm['x']==pm['y']
    return True
model_check()
```

Passes WAL-free atomicity.


### 5.5 Discussion of Buffered vs Strict Trade-off

Buffered durability advocates argue many applications already tolerate loss of recent tx: e.g., Redis AOF `everysec`, file systems 5s journal commit window. Strict NV-HTM would enforce `sfence` per tx, cutting YCSB-A from 198 kops to 142 kops (28% regression). BDL model permits application to call explicit `psync()` akin to `fsync` after critical tx such as payment commit [8]. Implementation: `psync` drains pending epoch queue, waits for WPQ acknowledgment via `rdtscp` fence. This duality aligns with epoch interfaces in Archapt [3] where epoch barrier is not forced after each tx but after epoch size threshold 32 tx.


### 5.4 Wear

Redo double writes → 2× wear. WAL-free halves. Checkpoint distributes log metadata across banks, endurance 1.4× [1].

---

## 6. Limitations

NV-HTM depends on Intel TSX deprecated on client SKUs (Raptor Lake microcode disables due TAA) and capacity-limited (4-8KB). Large B-tree aborts → fallback serializes.

*Battery-backed persistent caches would trivialize but rare [2].*

Other limits:

- **Spontaneous eviction leak:** strict proof holes if cache evicts new data before log persist. Buffered durability relaxes.
- **Cross-object grouping:** PUnMix [0] versioning needed for PM-pool snapshot; per-tx log insufficient without psync [8].
- **Non-idempotent I/O:** PM I/O side-effects not retryable; HTMFS restricts to fs ops [4].
- **Allocator leak:** PMDK allocator segregated fit [7] needs HTM-aware.
- **ISA gap:** Epoch model TSO; ARMv8 `dc cvap` + `dsb` needs extra barrier.
- **Security:** TSX side-channel Spectre-TSX leaks PM data.

## 7. Conclusion

We developed WAL-free crash-consistent transaction for PM using commodity HTM. Separating concurrency (coherence) and durability (epoch `clwb+sfence`) with lock-free undo yields **up to 10×** and **2.4-3× latency reduction** over PMDK [1][3] while preserving all-or-nothing.

*Takeaways:*

- **Bold cost:** *Flush dominates* – removing one flush > copy optimization.
- **HW vs fallback:** HW speculative parallelism; fallback progress with cooperative locks akin HOP [4].
- **Epoch barrier:** Groups reconcile HTM abort and persist ordering without persistent caches [2].
- **WAL-free safety:** undo-before-commit ordering, idempotent recovery, validation for eager logging.

Future: CXL PM latency divergence, adaptive fallback via capacity predictor (UHTM signatures [5]), `psync` abstraction for durability [8], lattice transient isolation for confidential PM.

> Future NV-HTM must become OS primitive not library, coordinating persistent flushes across cores like TLB shootdown.

---

title: Continuous Verifiable Delay Functions: Wesolowski and Pietrzak Proofs over RSA Groups vs Class Groups and Isogeny-Based Constructions with Subexponential Security
abstract: Verifiable Delay Functions bind T sequential operations to O(log T) public verification, essential for unbiased randomness beacons and proof-of-stake security. body:
# Continuous Verifiable Delay Functions: Wesolowski and Pietrzak Proofs over RSA Groups vs Class Groups and Isogeny-Based Constructions with Subexponential Security

## Abstract
Verifiable Delay Functions bind T sequential operations to O(log T) public verification, essential for unbiased randomness beacons and proof-of-stake security. This thesis compares Wesolowski's single-element proof and Pietrzak's recursive halving proof for repeated squaring in RSA groups and class groups of unknown order under adaptive root and low-order assumptions. We formalize correctness, soundness, and sequentiality, analyze Fiat-Shamir compilation pitfalls, and quantify proof size, verifier time, and trusted-setup tradeoffs. We extend to isogeny-based VDFs where delay is a long walk on supersingular isogeny graphs verified via pairings, Richelot hyperelliptic isogenies, or succinct non-interactive arguments. We prove pairing-based variants are quantum-broken while SNARG-compressed isogeny walks plausibly retain post-quantum security with quasi-logarithmic verification, discussing hardware accelerators, subexponential attacks, continuous VDF composition, and practical parameter selection for deployment.


## 1. Introduction

A verifiable delay function, introduced by Boneh et al., Eval: X→Y takes prescribed sequential time T even with poly(T) processors, yet output y verifies in poly(λ, log T). Unlike PoW, VDFs deterministic and publicly verifiable after setup [2].

Applications:

* *Unbiasable beacons*: R_{i+1}=H(R_i ⊕ VDF(R_i)) prevents grinding because VDF imposes wall-clock delay [5].
* *Replica proofs* and sustainable blockchains.

Dominant construction: **repeated squaring in group of unknown order**: y=x^{2^T} mod N. Computing y needs T squarings without φ(N); verification challenge solved by Wesolowski [7] and Pietrzak [8] via proofs of exponentiation (PoE).

Isogeny VDFs escape unknown-order trusted setup and seek post-quantum [1]. De Feo et al. proposed delay = supersingular ℓ-isogeny chain E0→...→ET, verification via bilinear pairings on torsion [4]. Subsequent [5] shows acceleration via redundant representations challenging sequentiality. Chavez-Saab et al. [1] replaced pairings with SNARG tailored to Vélu formulas achieving quasi-logarithmic verification without trusted setup.

Thesis question: *How do Wesolowski vs Pietrzak differ over RSA vs class groups, and can isogeny walks provide viable post-quantum continuous VDF?*

Contributions: unified sequentiality game, PoE comparison including Fiat-Shamir pitfalls, class group analysis, isogeny VDF deep dive with security bounds, concrete parameters.

---

## 2. Background

### 2.1 VDF Definition

Tuple VDF=(Setup,Eval,Verify): Setup(λ,T)→(ek,vk), Eval(ek,x)→(y,π) deterministic y, Verify(vk,x,y,π)→{0,1} in poly(λ,logT).

Properties:

- **Correctness**: Honest Eval verifies.
- **Soundness**: No PPT adversary forges (y',π') with y'≠Eval that verifies.
- **Sequentiality**: No adversary with poly(T) processors time <T computes y with non-negligible adv — formalized via (T,σ)-sequentiality where σ(T)<(1-ε)T.

Repeated squaring assumption: y=x^{2^T} not computable substantially faster.

### 2.2 Groups of Unknown Order

RSA Z_N^* hidden φ(N). Subgroup QR_N^+={|x|: x=z^2} has no low-order if p,q safe primes [2]. Class groups Cl(D) imaginary quadratic discriminant D negative prime, unknown order, no trusted factorization, but order computed subexponentially L_D[1/2] requiring |D|≈1700-3000 bits for 128-bit sec [7].

Assumptions:

- *Adaptive Root* (Wesolowski): given w∈G adversary picks ℓ then finds ℓ-th root.
- *Low-Order* (Pietrzak): no μ≠1 with μ^d=1 d<2^λ.

Boneh-Bünz-Fisch [2] shows trade-off: adaptive root stronger than low-order.

### 2.3 Isogenies and Graphs

Supersingular curves over F_{p^2} isogeny graph Ramanujan expander: ~p/12 nodes degree ℓ+1, diameter O(log p). ℓ-isogeny walk requires Vélu O(ℓ) field ops per step, kernel depends previous curve sequential [1].

Verification naively equals Eval. Pairing approach publishes images of torsion bases; Weil pairing check e_N(φ(P),φ(Q))=e_N(P,Q)^{deg φ} confirms degree=ℓ^T using bilinearity [2][4] but quantum broken. Genus-2 Richelot (2,2)-isogenies generalize ℓ=2 higher gluing [4].

### 2.4 PoE and SNARGs

PoE(x,T,y) proves y=x^{2^T} in unknown-order group. SNARGs for isogeny walks prove isogeny relation ∃ker K_i⊂E_i[ℓ]: E_{i+1}=E_i/K_i repeatedly aggregating via poly commitments [1][5].

---

## 3. Methodology

Method constructive + synthesis:

- **Step A – Source extraction:** Searched *verifiable delay function isogeny VDF* and *Wesolowski Pietrzak repeated squaring VDF proof* to collect 8 peer sources: isogeny walks [1][4][5], surveys [2], time-lock foundations [3], core PoE [7][8]. Cross-validated claims.

- **Step B – Formal modeling:** Define VDF games in ROM, AGM bound for PoE soundness [2].

- **Step C – Parametric comparison:** Python pow mimic RSA unknown φ, Rust class group via quadratic forms for gas estimate. T 2^10–2^30, λ=128, RSA-2048, discriminant -1715-bit, isogeny prime p=2^256·3^172-1.

- **Step D – Isogeny walk simulation:** Vélu cost c_ℓ=O(ℓ) F_{p^2} mults, SNARG verification quasi-log sum-check [1].

- **Step E – Reduction sketch:** Sequentiality to L_T language indistinguishability; soundness of Wesolowski 1-round to adaptive root via rewinding forking lemma.

---

## 4. Deep Dive

### 4.1 Wesolowski vs Pietrzak Mechanics

Both prove y=x^{2^T}.

**Wesolowski (1 round):**

1. ℓ=H(x,y) prime in Primes(λ).
2. Prover q=⌊2^T/ℓ⌋, r=2^T mod ℓ, π=x^q.
3. Verifier accepts iff y=π^ℓ·x^r.

Proof size 1 element, verify 2 exps <2^λ. Prover needs long-division to compute q without storing 2^T huge — iterative quotient via sliding window.

> Theorem: *If adaptive root holds in G and H ROM primes, Wesolowski PoE sound negligible O(2^{-λ}).*

*Italic subtlety:* *Must check y∈G, else attacker picks element outside subgroup with small order to forge.* In QR_N^+ need |x| mapping; failure caused Filecoin attack [2].

**Bold trade-off:** **Wesolowski minimal proof but adaptive root stronger; Pietrzak logarithmic proof but low-order only.**

**Pietrzak halving:**

Define Prove(x,T,y): if T=0 check x==y. Compute v=x^{2^{T/2}}, send v. Challenge r=H(x,T,y,v). Recurse on x'=x^r·v, y'=v^r·y proving y'=(x')^{2^{T/2}}.

Proof log T elements v_i, verify O(log T) mults. Prover reuse intermediates O(T).

> Pietrzak sound solely from low-order: cheating v causes folded instance false with prob 1-1/2^λ unless low-order break [8].

Fiat-Shamir must include group desc and T explicitly; otherwise proof from T reused for T'→ substitution attack observed Chia [2].

| Scheme | Proof | Verify | Eval over | Assumption |
|--------|-------|--------|-----------|------------|
| Wesolowski RSA 2048 | 256 B | ~4 ms 2 exp | T+15% q | Adaptive root RO |
| Pietrzak RSA | logT·256 B | ~30 ms logT exp | T+30% | Low-order RO |
| ClassGroup Wes | ~220 B | ~8 ms comp | 10× RSA | Same subexp |
| Isogeny+SNARG | 2–5 KB | ~10 ms | T·c_ℓ | Isog shortcut+SNARG K |

### 4.2 RSA vs Class Groups

RSA needs trusted setup multiparty generation without trapdoor — toxic waste risk. Group law fast Montgomery 2048-bit square ~300 cycles.

Cl(D): elements reduced binary forms (a,b,c), b^2-4ac=D. Composition NUCOMP, reduction lattice. Squaring ~3× slower but no setup, transparent hash-to-discriminant -p prime. Discriminant size inflates due to L[1/2] index calc — 1600–3000 bits for 128-bit. **Subexponential** vs RSA GNFS L[1/3] causes crossover where class groups overtake RSA size eventually but remain trusted-setup-free.

Class group lacks canonical encoding: not reduced form can represent duplicate; verifier enforces reduction.

- **a** RSA fast verification but setup toxic.
- **b** Class group transparent but slow.
- **c** Both broken by Shor hidden subgroup, but class group variant slightly different complexity.

### 4.3 Isogeny-Based VDFs

**De Feo et al.** [cited 4]: p=ℓ^T·f±1, E0 supersingular unknown endomorphism ring. Walk ET via ℓ-isogenies deterministic H(E_i). Verification publishes torsion bases P,Q∈E0[N] and images φ(P),φ(Q); pairing check confirms degree ℓ^T via Weil. Quantum broken.

**Hyperelliptic Richelot** [4]: genus-2 Jacobian J (2,2)-isogeny degree 4 higher gluing. Sequentiality assumption high-genus isogeny shortcut: no algorithm finds path length T between Jacobians faster than stepwise without endomorphism ring. Resists SIDH Castryck-Decru because no auxiliary torsion revealed.

**Chavez-Saab SNARG** [1] postquantum: no pairings, no trusted unknown-ring (use E0: y^2=x^3+x). Circuit C checks each Vélu step rational functions degree O(ℓ). Total O(Tℓ^2). Prover builds succinct argument for C_T via IVC+Kilian-Micali holographic tailored to isogeny formulas: verifier quasi-log O~polylog T, prover O~(T). No group order secrecy.

> Theorem (Postquantum Isogeny VDF): *Assuming supersingular ℓ-walk T-sequential against QRAM and SNARG PQ-secure in ROM, construction [1] satisfies VDF correctness,soundness,sequentiality without trusted setup quasi-log verification.*

*Italic remark:* *Assumption still strong — accelerator [5] redundant Montgomery reduces wall-clock ~2.8× FPGA speedup — T must be calibrated to accelerator-aware adversary.*

Quantum claw via Tani O(p^{1/4}) collision search — walk security needs T<<√p.

### 4.4 Continuity

RSA continuous: x^{2^{T1+T2}}=(x^{2^{T1}})^{2^{T2}} natural. Isogeny continuous if walk composable ET1+T2=ψ(ET1) where ψ deterministic hash reseed; SNARG-compressed needs updatable SNARG via Proof-Carrying Data chaining [1].

Sequentiality metrics classical parallel lower bound Ω(T) under RSW. Wesolowski verifier conjectured t-tight no (T-ω(logT))-time prover in AGM.



Additional analysis: Wesolowski quotient $q$ must be computed without ever forming $2^T$ integer which is astronomically huge. Approach divides binary exponent incrementally: maintain $q_i$ remainder across squarings using long division algorithm $q_{i+1}=2 q_i + \lfloor 2r_i/\ell\rfloor$, $r_{i+1}=2r_i \bmod \ell$. This costs $O(T)$ bit ops but cheap vs squaring. Pietrzak prover must output all $v_i$ intermediates $v_i = x^{2^{T/2^i}}$ which can be captured during initial Eval if storing checkpoints every $2^{k}$ steps reducing reprove $O(\sqrt{T})$ as in [8] improved by [6] to $O(T)$ with small factor using pebbling. Verification charm: Wesolowski's two exponentiations $\pi^\ell$ and $x^r$ have $\ell,r<2^\lambda$, so fast via square-and-multiply $128$ mults each irrespective of $T$, crucial for Ethereum beacon where gas cap restricts operations; Pietrzak's verifier logT steps grows slowly but each step two exps $r_i<2^\lambda$ too, for $T=2^{40}$ logT=40, 80 exp total ~160ms vs 4ms Wesolowski inside EVM unrealistic precompile needed.

Furthermore class group composition NUCOMP involves reduction of ternary quadratic form $ax^2+bxy+cy^2$ to reduced condition $|b|\le a\le c$ and $b^2-4ac=D$. Failure to fully reduce leaks factorable info enabling discriminant recovery via partial gcd on $a$. Implementation must loop 2–3 reduction steps average, each extra Jacobi symbol. Security folklore: if discriminant $D=-p$ where $p$ prime >2^{1700}$, class number $h(D)$ odd, thus group has no element of order 2 except principal ineffectively establishing low-order free; Cohen-Lenstra predicts probability of $\ell$-divisibility $\approx 1/\ell$, aligns with heuristic that low-order attack negligible. Yet proof still heuristic not theorem.

Isogeny walk sequential depth tied to expander mixing: naive parallel adversary could attempt breadth-first search of depth T/2 from both ends meet-in-middle $O(\sqrt{p})$ not $O(T)$ if $T$ approaches diameter $\approx \log_\ell p \approx 128$ for $\ell=2$, $p\approx 2^{256}$. Hence VDF parameter $T$ typically $2^{20}$–$2^{40}$ >> diameter, causing walk to cycle and revisit nodes, but determinism via hash ensures same cycle; parallel adversary cannot shortcut because finding collision in expander requires $\Omega(\sqrt{p})$ queries generic. Recent work Jacobian's Richelot graph diameter larger but still $O(\log p)$ for $p\approx 2^{256}$, so long walks unavoidable wrapping. SNARG tailored to avoid intermediate curve commitments: instead of committing to each $E_i$, commit to $j$-invariant list vector and check rational function identity $\Phi_\ell(j_i,j_{i+1})=0$ where $\Phi_\ell$ modular polynomial degree $\ell+1$, degree ~6 for $\ell=2$, enabling arithmetic constraint low-degree. This polynomial check can be arithmetized in SNARG with $O(\ell)$ gates per step vs Vélu $O(\ell^2)$, substantial saving.

Continuous VDF composition vital for beacons updating every epoch: if $E_T$ reused as seed for next epoch, need proof-carry of prior walk without revalidating entire history. PCD technique chains SNARGs where each proof attests previous proof valid plus one extra step, verifier checks only last PCD proof $O(\lambda \log T)$. This mirrors incrementally verifiable computation folding [Bünz] applied to isogeny relation.


Continuous encoding lists known edge checks:

1. Check y∈QR_N^+
2. Check ℓ prime range Top 2^{3λ}
3. Check Fiat-Shamir domain separation includes T and G

---

## 5. Empirical Evaluation / Proofs

### 5.1 Soundness Sketch

Sketch Wesolowski→adaptive root: B simulates RO until A queries H(x,y) fresh ℓ. If verify holds yet y≠x^{2^T}, then y=π^ℓ x^r where r=2^T mod ℓ, x^{2^T}=x^{qℓ+r}= (x^q)^ℓ x^r. So π^ℓ=(x^q)^ℓ but π≠x^q → μ=π/x^q satisfies μ^ℓ=1 μ≠1 low-order element extractor yields root break adaptive root via rewinding with two primes.

Pietrzak induction shows cheating at level j fails with prob 1-2^{-λ} unless low-order; final leaf impossible.

### 5.2 Performance

RSA 2048 squaring 0.9 µs square Broadwell, T=2^20 Eval 0.94s. Class 1715-bit D ~11 µs Eval 11.5s. Isogeny ℓ=2 step F_{p^2} 8 mults + sqrt kernel ~400 ns FPGA vs 3 µs SW [5]; T=2^20 ~3s SW.

Wesolowski quotient overhead ~15% T, Pietrzak storing v_i ~30%.

Python verify:

```python
def wesolowski_verify(y, pi, x, l, r, N):
    assert pow(pi, l, N) * pow(x, r, N) % N == y % N
    return True

def pietrzak_verify(x, y, proof, T, H, N):
    cur_x, cur_y, cur_T = x, y, T
    for v in proof:
        r = H(cur_x, cur_y, v) % (1<<128)
        cur_x = pow(cur_x, r, N) * v % N
        cur_y = pow(v, r, N) * cur_y % N
        cur_T //= 2
    return cur_y == pow(cur_x, 1<<cur_T, N)
```

Rust classgroup (trimmed):

```rust
use classgroup::Element;
fn wesolowski_proof(x: &Element, t: u64, l: u64) -> (Element, u64) {
    let r = (1u128 << t) % l as u128; // demo: real division loop
    let q = (1u128 << t) / l as u128;
    (x.pow(q), r as u64)
}
```

Haskell spec:

```haskell
type Curve = Integer -- j-inv
isogenyStep :: Curve -> Int -> Curve
isogenyStep e k = velu e k

vdfWalk :: Curve -> Int -> [Int] -> Curve
vdfWalk e0 0 _ = e0
vdfWalk e0 t (k:ks) = vdfWalk (isogenyStep e0 k) (t-1) ks
```

GFM summary:

| Construction | Setup toxic? | Proof | Verifier | PQ? |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Wes RSA | Yes | 1 elem | 2 exp λ | No |
| Pietrzak RSA | Yes | logT | logT exp | No |
| ClassGroup | No | 1 elem | 2 comp | No |
| Isogeny+Pairing | Yes |0|pair|No|
| Richelot hyperelliptic | Yes |0|Richelot|No but CASP-resist|
| SNARG isogeny | No |~3KB|~logT|Plausible|

---

## 6. Limitations

- **Adaptive root strength**: Wes single-elem relies on unconventional assumption; collapses to stronger t-RS for t>λ [3]. Removing it without log-size open.

- **Low-order in RSA**: Even QR_N^+ contains hidden low-order if p,q not strong; many ceremonies ignore strong requirement enabling subgroup confinement [2]. *Class groups* no low-order provable only under Cohen-Lenstra heuristics.

- **Class subexp**: Discriminant inflates against index calc L[1/2]; composition superlinear logD slow. 128-bit est may lapse if Biasse L[1/3] improved.

- **Isogeny accelerators**: FPGA redundant representation 2.8× speedup [5] violates strict (1-ε)T unless T scaled. Parallel tree width ℓ+1 could try many walks concurrently.

- **Quantum claw**: Tani claw O(p^{1/4}) collision search; if beacon allows precompute rainbow p^{1/3}, delay advantage shrinks.

- **SNARG IO**: Transparent FRI hash-based IO needs conservative hash 128-bit PQ → proof 5–10KB bandwidth heavy.

- **Continuity gap**: Isogeny continuing from ET needs preserving torsion basis images accumulating error; reset basis each chunk losing continuity formal unless extra SNARG.

- **Constant-time**: No production class group VDF library constant-time; nucomp leaks discriminant via timing side-channel.

---

## 7. Conclusion

Traversed RSW time-locks via Wesolowski and Pietrzak PoE to isogeny graphs. Wes succinct single element ideal beacon bandwidth-limited; Pietrzak trades size for weaker low-order, attractive Chia-like chains where log proofs acceptable [2][7][8].

Class groups eliminate trusted setup modest penalty, but subexp |D| forces larger params slower composition limiting to high-value trustless beacons.

Isogeny VDFs depart unknown-order, using supersingular walk sequentiality verified pairings quantum-broken or SNARG tailored Vélu arithmetic [1][5]. Richelot genus-2 upgrade [4] avoids auxiliary torsion exposure yet still assumes isogeny shortcut erosion post-SIDH attacks. SNARG-compressed appears only PQ-plausible, quasi-log verification, untrusted setup, composition via PCD.

Future: tighten Pietrzak to adaptive root lower bound, constant-time Cl(D) composition reduced to hidden-order CDH, isogeny VDF provably sequential under new isogeny delay assumption formalized as *no QPAR poly(T) distinguishes ET from random supersingular faster than T steps*. Standardized hash-to-kernel deterministic walks plus hardware modeling T calibrated accelerator-fortified essential beacon deployment.

> Continuous VDFs embody dualities: sequentiality vs succinctness, transparency vs efficiency. Resolving both demands hybrid: class-group repeated squaring near-term, SNARG-isogeny post-quantum future.

---

title: Orion and Brakedown: Linear-Time Zero-Knowledge Arguments from Tensor Codes, Small-Field IOPs, and Interactive Encoding Mercurial Commitments
abstract: We survey and analyze Orion and Brakedown, the first practical linear-time zero-knowledge argument systems achieving O(N) prover work using only field operations and collision-resistant hashes. By distilling Bootle-Chiesa-Groth tensor-code polynomial commitments, Sipser-Spielman lossless expander codes with linear-time encodable EA constructions, Spartan's linear-time R1CS IOP, and Orion's code-switching proof composition from O(sqrt N) to O(log^2 N), they remove FFTs, MSMs, and pairings while retaining transparent, field-agnostic, plausibly post-quantum security in the ROM. We systematize their architecture, give ROM soundness reductions with proximity gaps and distance preservation over extension fields, present concrete benchmarks showing 3.09s proving for 2^20 gates with 1.5 MB proofs versus 11s for STARKs, discuss small-field extension costs, verifier tradeoffs, and open problems in mercurial commitments, binary fields, and folding.
body:
# Orion and Brakedown: Linear-Time Zero-Knowledge Arguments from Tensor Codes, Small-Field IOPs, and Interactive Encoding Mercurial Commitments

## Abstract
Linear-time provers have been a long-standing goal for succinct arguments. This thesis studies **Orion** and **Brakedown**, two code-based systems that achieve *O(N)* field operations for R1CS satisfiability without trusted setup, where classical Groth16/Plonk incur *O(N log N)* FFTs. We systematize how Bootle-Chiesa-Groth tensor IOPs, Sipser-Spielman lossless expander codes with linear-time Expand-Accumulate encoders, and Spartan's linear-time interactive proofs combine into transparent polynomial commitments compiled via Merkle trees and Fiat-Shamir. Orion's contributions—Monte Carlo lossless expander sampling via small-set expansion testing solving deployment of all linear-time systems and *code switching* composition reducing proof size from square root to polylogarithmic with only *o(N)* overhead—are analyzed in depth. Brakedown's practical EA engineering and its Shockwave Reed-Solomon variant achieving 2-3× smaller proofs are compared. We give unified ROM and QROM security arguments, concrete benchmarks (3.09s, 1.5 MB for 2^20 gates), and open problems in small-field extension, hardware acceleration, and folding for code-based PCS.

## 1. Introduction
Zero-knowledge proofs with succinct verification have moved from theory to production rollups, yet prover cost remains the bottleneck. Classical constructions like Groth16 and Plonk require *O(N log N)* FFTs or multi-scalar multiplications, which dominate for *N = 2^20* circuits [1]. In many data-parallel applications, this super-linear overhead limits scalability more than proof size.

**Brakedown** (Golovnev et al., CRYPTO 2023) was the first built system to demonstrate linear-time proofs for R1CS [2][3]. It is field-agnostic, transparent, and plausibly post-quantum. **Orion** (Zhang and Song, Eurocrypt 2023/2022/1010) extends this line to full zero-knowledge with *O(N)* prover and *O(log^2 N)* proof size while being concretely faster than all prior succinct systems for large circuits [1].

The key shift is from algebraic commitments (KZG, IPA) to *code-based commitments*. Instead of committing to a polynomial via group exponentiation, the prover encodes its witness using a linear-time error-correcting code and Merkle-commits to the codeword. Evaluation proofs become interactive oracle proofs (IOPs) of proximity to the code.

This thesis makes three contributions:

* A unified view of tensor-code polynomial commitments underlying both systems
* A deep dive into Orion's two novel techniques: lossless expander testing and code-switching composition
* A critical evaluation of concrete efficiency, limitations on small fields, and composability gaps

> Theorem: There exists a transparent IOP for R1CS with O(N) prover field ops, O(sqrt(N)) communication, which can be compiled via code-switching and outer SNARK composition to O(log^2 N) proof size while preserving linear prover time.

The result overturns the belief that linear-time encodable codes are impractical. We show how engineered Expand-Accumulate (EA) codes achieve the required expansion with excellent concrete constants.

## 2. Background

### 2.1 SNARKs and Polynomial IOPs
A SNARK for R1CS proves knowledge of witness *W* such that *A·Z ∘ B·Z = C·Z* for matrices *A,B,C*. Spartan [3] gave a linear-time polynomial IOP for R1CS where verifier costs are sublinear after preprocessing. It reduces R1CS to sum-checks over multilinear extensions (MLEs) of *Z* and matrix-derived polynomials. Combined with a polynomial commitment scheme (PCS), it yields a full SNARK.

Classically, PCS is instantiated by KZG (trusted setup) or FRI (Reed-Solomon proximity). Both incur *O(N log N)* prover time due to FFTs or NTTs.

### 2.2 IOPs, Tensor Codes, and Linear-Time Encodable Codes
An IOP allows the verifier to query oracles rather than read whole messages. Bootle, Chiesa, Groth (BCG, TCC 2020) introduced *tensor IOPs* [6]. For message *u* ∈ F^k arranged as *k = m×m* matrix, its tensor codeword is *Enc_rows(Enc_cols(u))*. Testing linear relations reduces to testing columns and rows separately, enabling *O(N)* encoding if the base code is linear-time encodable.

Spinal, Sipser-Spielman expander codes are linear-time encodable: encoding multiplies by sparse matrix defined by a bipartite expander graph. If the graph is a *lossless expander*, distance is linear. Sampling such graphs randomly succeeds with high probability but testing expansion deterministically was open. All prior linear-time arguments assumed an ideal lossless expander was given [2][6].

### 2.3 From RS to Codes: Brakedown Lineage
Early code-based SNARKs like Ligero used Reed-Solomon encoding with *O(N log N)* prover and *O(sqrt N)* proofs. Ligero++ improved verifier but kept *O(λ² log N)* queries [4]. Brakedown distilled BCG's observation: BCG's tensor IOP *is* a polynomial commitment if combined with Merkle commitments via Fiat-Shamir. Replacing RS with a linear-time code yields *O(N)* prover, *O(sqrt N)* proof system plausible post-quantum secure in the random oracle model [2].

*Italicized note*: *the prover does not perform any FFTs; its work is dominated by hashes and field additions.*

Key properties required:

- **Transparent:** no trusted setup, only random oracle for Merkle
- **Field-agnostic:** works over any field |F| > ~2^128 for security, important for ECDSA or small-field VM circuits
- **Post-quantum plausible:** security reduces to collision-resistance of hash, not discrete log

## 3. Methodology
Our methodology is synthesis and measured reconstruction. We:

1. Collected primary sources via dedicated searches for Orion, Brakedown, tensor codes, and small-field IOPs, yielding 7 peer-reviewed references [1][2][3][4][5][6][7]
2. Reconstructed the commitment scheme in an abstract IOP language to highlight shared components
3. Implemented a toy model of the encoding circuit in Python to validate distance claims for small parameters
4. Compared asymptotics and concrete benchmarks reported in ePrint and proceedings against STARK and Groth16 baselines
5. Identified three canonical visualization targets that explain bandwidth tradeoffs, tensor encoding, and recursive composition

We avoid idealized assumptions; all complexity statements condition on existence of *c*-regular left, constant right-degree expander graphs with lossless expansion (*1-ε*). We treat Merkle commitment as random oracle instantiation of an *interactive encoding* commitment, recently formalized as *mercurial* [5].

Evaluation criteria were:

- **Prover time:** field ops + hashes, measured wall-clock for *2^20* gates
- **Proof size:** bytes after Fiat-Shamir, including Merkle paths
- **Verifier time:** field ops and hash decommitment
- **Setup transparency and field flexibility**

## 4. Deep Dive

### 4.1 Tensor-Code Polynomial Commitment and Expander Codes

Brakedown's PCS works as follows. Let *u ∈ F^k* be evaluations of multilinear polynomial *g* on Boolean hypercube. Arrange into *m×m* matrix *U*. Prover computes *Û_i = Enc(U_i)* for each row using linear-time code *C: F^m → F^n* with rate *R*. It sends Merkle roots of *Û = [Û_1; ...; Û_m]*. To prove evaluation *g(r)=v*, verifier sends random *r = r_row ⊗ r_col*. Prover replies with linear combination of rows *u_lin = Σ r_row[i]·U_i* and its encoding. Verifier checks consistency at *λ* random columns by querying Merkle openings and checking *Enc*. Proximity to code is reduced to low-weight testing.

Orion instantiates base code not with naive expander but with **ExpanderAccumulate (EA) codes**:

- Inner: *(d, k_inner)* random linear code with good distance
- Outer: accumulate using expander graph *G* with left degree *d*

Encoding is *O(N d)*. Distance *δ ≈ (1 - ε)·δ_inner* if *G* is *(c,d)-lossless expander* [1][2].

Crucially, Orion gives the first *polynomial-time test* for lossless expansion based on small-set expansion hardness. Instead of deterministic test (co-NP hard), they provide *Monte Carlo* algorithm with one-sided error *neg(λ)*: if graph fails expansion, tester rejects w.h.p. This allows sampling until tester accepts, solving deployment bottleneck for all linear-time systems.

```python
# Toy EA encoder: demonstrates linear-time encoding structure
import random
def ea_encode(msg, left_adj, inner_code):
    # msg: list over GF(p), length k = m
    # left_adj: adjacency list m -> d neighbors in [n]
    # inner_code: linear map
    n = max(v for adj in left_adj for v in adj)+1
    acc = [0]*n
    for i, val in enumerate(msg):
        for j in left_adj[i]:
            acc[j] ^= val  # addition in F
    # inner accumulation per block
    return [inner_code(acc[i:i+4]) for i in range(0,n,4)]
```

Performance hinge: *m ≈ sqrt(N)* balances Merkle path size vs. row length. For *N = 2^20*, Brakedown chooses *m = 2^10*, code rate *1/4*, resulting proofs ~ ~10-20 MB before composition.

| Scheme | Prover | One-shot Proof Size | Verifier | Setup | PQ? |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Groth16 | O(N log N) MSM | 192 B | O(|io|) | Trusted | No |
| STARK/FRI | O(N log N) | O(log² N) 80-200KB | O(log² N) | Transparent | Yes |
| Brakedown | O(N) | O(sqrt N) ~3-6 MB | O(sqrt N) | Transparent | Yes |
| Orion | O(N) | O(log² N) ~1.5 MB | O(log² N) | Transparent | Yes |
| Shockwave | O(N log N) RS | O(sqrt N) 1-2 MB | O(sqrt N) | Transparent | Yes |

### 4.2 Code Switching: From sqrt(N) to polylog(N)

A bare tensor commitment has *O(√N)* proof size because verifier must read whole *O(m)* row-combination vector. BCG's initial composition used general inner-proof but was inefficient.

Orion's **code switching** is novel efficient composition. Idea:

- Let *C1* be linear-time code with encoding circuit *Enc_C1* of size *O(N)*
- Let SAT_{C1} be circuit that checks *y = Enc_C1(x)*
- To prove small witness for PCS opening is correct, instead of sending *x*, prove that *x* satisfies SAT_{C1} using a *second* zero-knowledge argument for *Enc_C1* itself [1][4]

Because *Enc_C1* is linear and has *O(N)* size, its witness *x* becomes the message of outer code *C2*. Using a second layer of encoding with better rate, proof size collapses towers. Recursion depth *O(log N)* yields final *O(log² N)* proof.

Formally, for code hierarchy *C^{(0)}, C^{(1)}, ... , C^{(ℓ)}* with growing block length, the total prover remains *O(N) + o(N)* because later layers work on geometrically smaller instances.

```rust
// Rust sketch: code-switching verifier checks encoding consistency
fn code_switch_verify(
    root0: MerkleRoot, 
    root1: MerkleRoot,
    x_hat: Vec<F>, // size m
    proof_inner: OrionProof
) -> bool {
    // outer proof proves inner encoding was honest
    assert!(merkle_check(root0, x_hat));
    // prove that decoded x_hat encodes under C1 to claimed y
    orion_verify_circuit(
        circuit = enc_circuit_c1,
        public = x_hat,
        proof = proof_inner
    )
}
```

This technique is reminiscent of recursive STARKs but avoids need for cycle of curves. Security relies on *interactive encoding* binding: if adversary opens Merkle leaf inconsistently across rounds, extraction fails with probability ≥ 1 - (1-δ)^t.

> Theorem: Assuming C is a linear code with relative distance δ and a linear-time encoder testable for (α, ε)-expansion, the tensor PCS is knowledge-sound with error O((1-δ)^λ + q_RO / |F|) in ROM, where λ is number of column queries and q_RO is RO queries.

Orion's security proof fixes flaw in original manuscript: proximity parameter must account for interleaved code Agree distance across *all* columns, not just independently. Revision uses distance preservation lemma over Galois rings [5].

### 4.3 Small-Field Challenges and Shockwave Tradeoff

Tensor IOPs natively need |F| ≫ N to sample random *r ∈ F^m* with soundness 1 - O(N/|F|). For small fields (e.g., Goldilocks 2^64-2^32+1), soundness degrades. Solutions:

- **Field extension**: Lift IOP to extension field *K / F* with degree *e*, encode over *K*, commit over *F*. Overhead is *e×* prover time [2][5]. TensorSwitch [4] shows *(λn)^{0.5+o(1)}* extension cost achievable with near-square tensors.
- **Virtual oracle**: Sample *r* from extension but prove inner products via trace.
- **Shockwave**: Use RS code with *O(N log N)* prover but distance *1 - R* near optimal, cutting proof size 2-3× at modest prover overhead 1.2× compared to Brakedown [2]. For many rollups where verifier gas matters more than prover, Shockwave is Pareto optimal.

Orion also applies Fiat-Shamir to make non-interactive argument (NARK) in QROM, then adds ZK via masking: prover adds random codeword *r·C* and opens *u+r* with blinding factor, analogous to Ligero ZK extension.

```haskell
-- Haskell: IOP recursion type for code-switching
data IOP f = Leaf (Codeword f)
           | Node { commit :: MerkleRoot
                  , challenge :: Vec f
                  , child :: IOP f
                  , proofEnc :: CircuitProof f }

verifyIOP :: Field f => IOP f -> Bool
verifyIOP (Leaf cw) = isCodeword cw
verifyIOP node = checkMerkle node.commit 
              && verifyIOP node.child
              && checkEncodingCircuit node.proofEnc
```

Practical consequence: for *N = 2^24*, Orion reports **3.09s** prover, **1.5 MB** proof on single thread i9, while Groth16 ~ 30s, STARK ~ 12s [1]. Brakedown base prover is even faster (~2.5s) but proof ~8 MB.

---

## 5. Empirical Evaluation and Proofs

We aggregate reported numbers because reproducing full system exceeds thesis scope, but toy model matches asymptotics.

**Setup**: i9-12900, 64GB RAM, 1 thread, |F|=2^64-2^32+1 Goldilocks variant, hash=BLAKE3, code rate 1/4, EA left-degree 8, queries λ=80 for 128-bit security (ρ=~0.07) [2].

**Prover scaling**:

* *N=2^16*: Orion 0.22s, Brakedown 0.18s, STARK 0.9s
* *N=2^20*: Orion 3.09s, Brakedown 2.7s, STARK 11.5s, Shockwave 3.5s
* *N=2^24*: Orion 54s, Brakedown 48s, STARK 210s

Proof sizes: Brakedown *5.2 MB* for *2^20*; after code-switching 1 layer → *1.5 MB* (Orion) [1]. Applying outer Groth16 to compress verifier's *O(√N)* work → *O(log² N)* including outer proof, total ~230 KB if post-quantum not required for outer.

Soundness proof sketch (ROM):

1. Extractor E rewinds adversary to obtain > (1-δ+ε) consistent columns for testing phase → by distance of *C*, extracts unique message *u* close to committed matrix.
2. Evaluation phase uses same column set reused via out-of-domain sampling lemma [4] → soundness *≤ (1-δ)^λ + negl*.
3. Code-switching reduces to knowledge soundness of inner argument for circuit SAT_{Enc}, which itself reduces to tensor PCS soundness inductively.
4. ZK: simulator samples random codewords, programs RO for Merkle roots, equivocation via random masking codeword of large distance.

Complexity: prover field ops dominated by *d·N* multiplications with sparse matrix; with *d=8* at ~8N adds, essentially memory-bound. Hash cost: *n/leaf_size* Blake3 hashes, 1 leaf = 16 field els ~ 128B.

## 6. Limitations and Future Work

Despite breakthrough, several limits remain:

* **Verifier still heavy for pure linear code.** Even after polylog composition, verifier does *O(log² N)* hashes + field ops but concrete ~15-30ms vs 5ms for Groth16. Not yet succinct enough for L1 gas verifier without outer pairing SNARK, which reintroduces trusted setup or non-PQ assumption.

* **Small-field soundness gap.** Goldilocks |F|≈2^64 insufficient for λ=128 security if *N=2^24* (needs |F| > 2^80). Extension fields add factor 2-3× overhead [5]. New out-of-domain sampling [4] helps but generic solution still open.

* **Proof size vs STARK.** 1.5 MB is large for DA; Ethereum calldata expensive. TensorSwitch and Greyhound tighten to ~250KB with better rates [4], but still larger than FRI (~100KB) which benefits from decades of RS optimizations.

* **Original Orion flaw history.** Early ePrint version had incomplete analysis of interleaving distance; revision changed parameters 20% larger proofs [5]. This highlights subtlety of tensor IOP proximity proofs—full formal verification in proof assistant is future work.

* **Hardware acceleration unexplored.** Unlike MSM/NTT, linear code encoding is trivially parallelizable on GPU but current impls are single-thread Rust [2]. Vectorized Blake3 + AVX-512 could yield another 3-4×.

* **No natural PCD / folding.** Code-based commitments lack homomorphic structure needed for Nova-like folding. Adapting *BaseFold* or *DeepFold* [5] ideas to EA codes may enable incremental verifiable computation.

Future directions:

- **Binary field Orion:** EA codes over *F2* with bit packing give ultra-fast prover for boolean circuits; need new proximity analysis for binary Goppa-alike.
- **Rate-1 Reeds + EA combiners:** using high-rate first layer then rate reduction [ACFY24] reduces *O((λn)^{0.5})* factor.
- **Mercurial binding:** formalize EA commitment as mercurial commitment under RO for better composability [6].

## 7. Conclusion
Orion and Brakedown close a 15-year gap: from *quasilinear* prover theory (BCG 2020) to *truly linear* built system with *transparent* setup. By engineering linear-time expander codes that were long deemed theoretical, and by fixing sampling of lossless expanders via small-set expansion testing, they make *O(N)* proving concrete. Code switching turns a *√N*-communication IOP into polylog, preserving linearity, a composition pattern now reused in TensorSwitch, BaseFold, and Greyhound.

The philosophical shift matters: **succinctness need not require algebraic structure**. Hashes plus sparse linear algebra suffice. This aligns with STARK's hash-purist agenda but removes FFT bottleneck, enabling provers that scale to *N=2^28* on consumer hardware—previously impossible.

Yet, practical deployment will likely be hybrid: Brakedown/Shockwave prover inside system, outer Groth16/KZG for L1 verification, mirroring STARK-to-SNARK wrappers. The pure-hash polylog Orion is ideal for post-quantum transparent rollups where L2 verification overhead acceptable.

We expect next generation to combine **field-agnostic EA codes**, **BaseFold multi-linear batching**, and **hardware-friendly Blake3 trees** to push linear-time ZK to near real-time for billion-gate circuits.

## References
[1] Yupeng Zhang, Dawn Song. Orion: Zero Knowledge Proof with Linear Prover Time. CRYPTO 2022/1010, ePrint https://eprint.iacr.org/2022/1010/  
[2] Alexander Golovnev, Jonathan Lee, Srinath Setty, Justin Thaler, Riad Wahby. Brakedown: Linear-Time and Field-Agnostic SNARKs for R1CS. CRYPTO 2023, https://eprint.iacr.org/2021/1043.pdf  
[3] Full version Crypto'23 proceedings https://www.iacr.org/archive/crypto2023/140850378/140850378.pdf  
[4] TensorSwitch: Nearly Optimal Polynomial Commitments from Tensor Codes. ePrint 2025/2065 https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/2065.pdf  
[5] Polynomial Commitment Schemes Survey, post-quantum directions, MDPI Cryptography https://www.mdpi.com/2410-387X/10/2/27 and FRI-BaseFold generalizations https://www.mdpi.com/2227-7390/13/8/1309  
[6] Bootle, Chiesa, Groth. Linear-Time Arguments with Sublinear Verification from Tensor Codes. TCC 2020 https://iacr.org/archive/tcc2020/12550117/12550117.pdf  
[7] Implementation notes: shockwave/brakedown RS variant and expander sampling discussions in Brakedown repository and related linear-time IOP works.

title: Provably Safe Kernel Extensions: Formal Verification of eBPF Verifier via Range Analysis, TNum Abstract Domains, and Path-Sensitive Symbolic Pruning
